paraphrases.simplest: Я не знаю. — dropping даже gives a more neutral phrasing.

takeaway.note: A high-frequency particle citing an extreme example for emphasis, often in negated sentences.

skeleton.note: interrogative particle, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: разве is an interrogative particle carrying surprise or doubt.

grammarFocus.construction: разве ('surely not,' doubt particle) + не знаешь (negated imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Разве ('really? surely not') expresses the speaker's surprise/doubt, combining with the negated question не знаешь ('don't you know').

options.note: неужели ('is it really possible') is an even stronger synonym for surprise.
правда ('really') is a more neutral confirmation.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты не знаешь? — dropping разве gives a plainer question.

takeaway.note: A high-frequency interrogative particle expressing surprise at an unexpected fact, often with negated questions.

skeleton.note: emphatic particle "exactly", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: именно means "exactly/precisely".

grammarFocus.construction: именно ('exactly,' emphasizing particle) + demonstrative это
grammarFocus.note: Именно ('exactly, precisely') emphasizes the adjacent word, here emphasizing это ('this'), which is followed by хочу ('I want').

options.ru: Это именно то, что я хочу.
options.note: то, что ('the thing that') adds a relative clause for clarity.
ровно ('exactly') is another emphasizing word.

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу это. — dropping именно gives a more neutral phrasing.

takeaway.note: A high-frequency particle for emphasizing a specific thing being pointed to.

skeleton.note: restrictive particle "only", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: лишь is a more literary synonym of только.

grammarFocus.construction: лишь ('only,' restrictive particle) + infinitive спать
grammarFocus.note: Лишь ('only, merely') is a more literary synonym for только, restricting the imperfective infinitive спать ('to sleep').

options.note: только ('only,' more colloquial) is a synonym.
сон ('sleep,' noun) is used instead.

paraphrases.simplest: Хочу только спать. — dropping the subject gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: Nearly synonymous with только but more literary/formal in register.

skeleton.note: colloquial hedging particle "seems like", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: вроде is a colloquial particle expressing "it seems like".

grammarFocus.construction: вроде ('seems like,' conjecture particle) + zero copula + nominative хороший человек
grammarFocus.note: Вроде ('kind of, seems like') marks an uncertain impression; no быть appears between он and хороший человек ('a good person') in the present tense.

variations.note: Subject changed to feminine, though хороший often stays masculine in this fixed phrase; speakers usually rephrase as она хорошая девушка, etc.

options.note: казаться ('to seem') is a more formal phrasing.
по-моему ('in my opinion') is a more personal take.

paraphrases.simplest: Он хороший человек. — dropping вроде gives a more assertive phrasing.

takeaway.note: A high-frequency colloquial particle expressing an uncertain impression, nearly synonymous with кажется.

keyPoint: без is a preposition requiring the genitive, meaning "without".

grammarFocus.construction: не могу (impossibility construction) + без + genitive тебя
grammarFocus.note: Не могу ('I can't') is followed by без ('without') plus the genitive тебя ('you'), expressing 'I can't [live] without you' — the infinitive (жить, etc.) is omitted.

variations.note: Subject changed to feminine, object to masculine него.

options.ru: Я не могу жить без тебя.
options.note: Spells out the omitted жить ('to live').
необходим ('essential') is an alternative.

paraphrases.simplest: Не могу без тебя. — dropping the subject gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: Без always requires the genitive; a high-frequency fixed phrase for emotional dependency.

keyPoint: через + accusative expresses "in [X amount of time]".

grammarFocus.construction: через + accusative (in..., time preposition) + приду (perfective future)
grammarFocus.note: Через ('in, after') requires the accusative, here combining with час (masculine, 'an hour'), and co-occurs with the perfective future придёт of прийти ('to come').

options.note: буду ('I'll be') is a shorter phrasing.
у тебя ('at your place') is a more colloquial arrival expression.

paraphrases.simplest: Через час приду. — dropping the subject gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: An important preposition expressing elapsed time until a future point.

keyPoint: после is a preposition requiring the genitive, meaning "after".

grammarFocus.construction: после + genitive (after) + иду (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: После ('after') requires the genitive, here работы (genitive of работа). Идти ('to go') is imperfective, expressing present movement.

options.note: закончив ('having finished,' a gerund) is more written.

options.ru: С работы я иду прямо домой.
options.note: с работы ('from work') is an alternative construction.

paraphrases.simplest: После работы домой. — dropping иду gives a more casual phrasing.

takeaway.note: An important time preposition contrasting with до ('before'), always taking the genitive.

keyPoint: перед is a preposition requiring the instrumental, meaning "before".

grammarFocus.construction: перед + instrumental (before) + читаю (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Перед ('before,' time/position) requires the instrumental, here сном (instrumental of сон, 'sleep'). Читать ('to read') is imperfective, habitual.

options.ru: Я читаю перед тем, как лягу спать.
options.note: перед тем, как ('before,' as a subordinate clause) is more explicit.

options.ru: Перед сном у меня привычка читать.
options.note: привычка ('habit') is a noun-based phrasing.

paraphrases.simplest: Перед сном читаю. — dropping the subject gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: An important preposition for position/time, always taking the instrumental.

keyPoint: между is a preposition requiring the instrumental, meaning "between".

grammarFocus.construction: между + instrumental plural (between) + стоишь (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Между ('between') requires the instrumental, here столами (instrumental plural of стол, 'table'). Стоять ('to stand') is a stative verb.

options.note: находиться ('to be located,' more formal) is an alternative.
посередине ('in the middle') adds specificity.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты между столами? — dropping стоишь gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: An important preposition for position among two or more things, always taking the instrumental.

keyPoint: под + instrumental expresses a static location "under" (motion takes the accusative instead).

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + под + instrumental (under) столом
grammarFocus.note: Под ('under') requires the instrumental for a static location, here столом (instrumental of стол). No быть appears in the present tense.

variations.note: Subject changed to the feminine кошка ('cat').

options.note: лежать ('to lie') specifies the posture.
спрятаться ('to hide') focuses on the action.

paraphrases.simplest: Собака под столом. — the simplest phrasing as is.

takeaway.note: Important: под takes the instrumental for static location (it takes the accusative for motion toward).

keyPoint: смеяться над + instrumental is the fixed construction for "to laugh at".

grammarFocus.construction: над + instrumental (about, in 'to laugh at') + смеёшься (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Над ('over/at') requires the instrumental; in this context, смеяться над ('to laugh at') is a fixed construction with этим (instrumental of это).

options.note: смешно ('funny,' impersonal predicate) is an alternative construction.
находить ('to find') plus смешным (instrumental, 'funny') is another phrasing.

paraphrases.simplest: Смеёшься над этим? — dropping ты gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: A fixed construction for 'laughing at/mocking'; над always takes the instrumental here.

keyPoint: около is a preposition requiring the genitive, meaning "near".

grammarFocus.construction: около + genitive (near) + живу (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Около ('near, close to') requires the genitive, here метро (invariable noun). Жить ('to live') is imperfective, habitual residence.

options.note: рядом с ('right next to,' instrumental) is an alternative construction.
близко от ('close to') flips the perspective.

paraphrases.simplest: Живу около метро. — dropping the subject gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: An important proximity preposition, nearly synonymous with рядом с (instrumental), always taking the genitive.

keyPoint: против is a preposition requiring the genitive, meaning "against".

grammarFocus.construction: против + genitive (against) меня
grammarFocus.note: Против ('against') requires the genitive, here меня ('me'). No быть appears in the present tense.

options.ru: Ты на моей стороне или нет?
options.note: на моей стороне ('on my side') asks from the opposite angle.
не согласен ('don't you agree') is an alternative.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты против? — dropping меня gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: An important preposition for opposition, contrasting with за ('for,' accusative), always taking the genitive.

skeleton.note: preposition "for the sake of", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: ради is a preposition requiring the genitive, expressing a devoted motive, "for the sake of".

replies.gloss: I'm willing to do the same.

grammarFocus.construction: ради + genitive (for the sake of) тебя + делаю (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Ради ('for the sake of') requires the genitive and carries a stronger nuance of devotion/sacrifice than для ('for'); here it combines with тебя ('you').

options.note: для ('for,' more neutral) is a milder alternative.
из-за ('because of') carries a different, causal nuance.

paraphrases.simplest: Делаю это ради тебя. — dropping the subject gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.pattern: ради + genitive (for the sake of, devotion)
takeaway.note: An important preposition carrying a stronger nuance of sacrifice/devotion than the more neutral для; always takes the genitive.

keyPoint: кроме is a preposition requiring the genitive, meaning "except".

grammarFocus.construction: никого (negative pronoun) + не зовёшь (negated imperfective) + кроме + genitive меня
grammarFocus.note: Никого ('nobody,' genitive) always co-occurs with не; кроме ('except') requires the genitive меня ('me'). Звать ('to call/invite') is imperfective.

variations.ru: Она никого не зовёт, кроме меня?
Вы никого не зовёте, кроме меня?

options.note: только ('only') gives a near-positive phrasing.

options.ru: Кроме меня, ты зовёшь кого-то ещё?
options.note: Reordering asks whether anyone else is involved.

paraphrases.simplest: Зовёшь только меня? — a shorter, more natural phrasing.

takeaway.note: An important preposition for exclusion, always taking the genitive; никого не...кроме expresses a strong 'nobody but' restriction.

skeleton.note: preposition "instead of", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: вместо is a preposition requiring the genitive, meaning "instead of".

grammarFocus.construction: imperative иди (imperfective) + вместо + genitive (instead of)
grammarFocus.note: Вместо ('instead of') requires the genitive, here меня ('me'). Иди is the imperative of идти ('to go').

variations.note: The one being replaced changed to него ('him').

options.note: за ('in place of,' accusative) is an alternative construction.
заменить ('to substitute/replace') is used instead.

paraphrases.simplest: Иди за меня. — swapping вместо for за gives a nearly identical phrasing.

takeaway.note: An important preposition for substitution/replacement, always taking the genitive.

skeleton.note: preposition "in the presence of", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: при is a preposition requiring the prepositional case, meaning "in the presence of / at the time of".

grammarFocus.construction: не + imperative говори (imperfective) + при + prepositional (in the presence of)
grammarFocus.note: Negated commands typically use the imperfective (говори, the imperative of говорить). При ('in the presence of') requires the prepositional, here детях (prepositional plural of дети).

options.note: в присутствии ('in the presence of') is a more written phrase.
States directly that the kids mustn't hear it.

paraphrases.simplest: Не говори перед детьми. — swapping при for перед gives a near-identical phrasing.

takeaway.note: An important preposition for something happening in someone's presence, always taking the prepositional.

keyPoint: про is a colloquial preposition requiring the accusative, meaning "about".

grammarFocus.construction: imperative расскажи (perfective) + про + accusative (about)
grammarFocus.note: Про ('about') is a colloquial near-synonym of о, requiring the accusative (свой день, 'your day'). Расскажи is the imperative of the perfective рассказать ('to tell, once').

options.note: о ('about,' prepositional) is a more standard phrasing.
как прошёл ('how did it go') is a more general way to ask.

paraphrases.simplest: Расскажи о дне. — swapping про for о and dropping свой gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: A colloquial synonym of о ('about,' prepositional) — differs by requiring the accusative.

keyPoint: насчёт is a preposition requiring the genitive, meaning "regarding/about".

grammarFocus.construction: interrogative что + насчёт + genitive (about) + думаешь (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Насчёт ('regarding, about') requires the genitive, here кофе (an invariable noun used genitively). Думать ('to think') is a stative imperfective.

options.note: о ('about,' prepositional) is more standard.
как насчёт ('how about') is a shorter, suggestion-like phrasing.

paraphrases.simplest: Как насчёт кофе? — dropping думаешь gives a concise suggestion.

takeaway.note: A colloquial synonym of о ('about'), always taking the genitive.

keyPoint: пока means "still/for now" and is also used as a farewell.

grammarFocus.construction: пока ('for now') + не уходишь (negated imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Пока ('for now, yet') marks a temporary state, combining with the negated present of уходить ('to leave').

options.note: ещё ('still') plus здесь ('here') is a shorter confirmation.
Negating торопиться ('to hurry') is an alternative.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты не уходишь? — dropping пока gives a more direct phrasing.

takeaway.note: A high-frequency adverb marking 'for the time being.'

keyPoint: потому что is a causal conjunction meaning "because".

replies.gloss: Too bad you couldn't make it.

grammarFocus.construction: потому что ('because,' causal conjunction) + был занят (past of быть + short-form adjective)
grammarFocus.note: Потому что ('because') introduces the reason; был занят ('was busy') requires быть explicit in the past tense, combined with the short-form adjective занят.

variations.ru: Она не пришла, потому что была занята.
Мы не пришли, потому что были заняты.

options.note: из-за ('because of') plus the noun занятость ('busyness').

options.ru: Я был занят, поэтому не пришёл.
options.note: поэтому ('therefore') reverses the cause-effect order.

paraphrases.simplest: Не пришёл, был занят. — dropping потому что gives a more colloquial juxtaposition.

takeaway.note: The basic conjunction introducing a cause/reason, contrasting with поэтому ('therefore,' result).

skeleton.note: conjunctive adverb "therefore", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: поэтому is a conjunctive adverb expressing a consequence, "therefore".

grammarFocus.construction: поэтому ('therefore,' result conjunction) + не могу (impossibility construction)
grammarFocus.note: Поэтому ('therefore') introduces a result, here linking занят ('busy') from the previous clause to не могу ('I can't').

options.ru: Я занят, так что не могу.
options.note: так что ('so') is a synonymous conjunction.
из-за ('because of') is more written.

paraphrases.simplest: Занят, не могу. — dropping поэтому gives a more colloquial juxtaposition.

takeaway.note: The basic conjunction introducing a result, contrasting with потому что ('because,' cause).

keyPoint: хотя is a concessive conjunction meaning "although".

replies.gloss: Why go if you don't want to?
I'll come with you if needed.

grammarFocus.construction: хотя ('although,' concessive conjunction) + не хочу (negated imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Хотя ('although') links the fact of going (иду) with the conflicting feeling of не хочу ('don't want to').

options.ru: Я иду, несмотря на то что не хочу.
options.note: несмотря на то что ('despite the fact that') is a more written concessive phrase.
Using но ('but') reverses the order, more colloquially.

paraphrases.simplest: Иду, но не хочу. — swapping хотя for но gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: The basic conjunction linking a fact with an unexpected/contrasting circumstance.

skeleton.note: conjunction "as if", this sentence's target word

keyPoint: будто is a comparative conjunction meaning "as if".

grammarFocus.construction: будто ('as if,' hypothetical/comparative conjunction) + знаешь (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Будто ('as if') expresses an unreal comparison/supposition, modifying the claim всё знаешь ('know everything') as if it were true.

options.ru: Ты говоришь, как будто всё знаешь.
options.note: как будто ('as if,' stronger) is a near-synonym.

options.ru: Ты делаешь вид, что всё знаешь.
options.note: делать вид ('to pretend') is a fixed phrase.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты говоришь, как будто знаешь. — dropping всё gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: An important conjunction for unreal comparison/supposition, nearly synonymous with как будто.

keyPoint: правда functions both as the noun "truth" and the adverb "really".

grammarFocus.construction: правда ('really,' confirming adverb) + видел (perfective past)
grammarFocus.note: Правда ('really') functions as a doubt/confirmation adverb, combining with the perfective past of видеть ('to see, a single sighting').

options.note: точно ('for sure') is a more standard confirmation.
серьёзно ('seriously') is more casual.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты это видел? — dropping правда gives a plainer question.

takeaway.note: A high-frequency adverb for emphasizing doubt/confirmation in questions.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: вопрос is a regular hard-stem masculine noun.

grammarFocus.construction: у меня есть (affirmative possession) + nominative вопрос
grammarFocus.note: У меня есть ('I have') is the basic possession construction; the object вопрос ('question') takes the nominative (contrast with the negated у меня нет, which takes the genitive).

options.note: спросить ('to ask') is more action-oriented.
задать вопрос ('to pose a question') plus можно is more polite.

paraphrases.simplest: Есть вопрос. — dropping у меня gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: An extremely common construction for 'X has Y' — the object stays nominative, unlike the negated у меня нет (genitive).

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: ответ is a regular hard-stem masculine noun.

replies.gloss: I think I know it too.

grammarFocus.construction: знаю (imperfective) + accusative ответ
grammarFocus.note: Знать ('to know') is imperfective, expressing an ongoing state; ответ (masculine inanimate, same as nominative) is the accusative object.

options.note: известен ('is known,' short-form adjective) is more written.
у меня есть ('I have') is an alternative construction.

paraphrases.simplest: Знаю ответ. — dropping the subject gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: The basic pattern for stating the object of knowledge directly in the accusative.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: проблема is a regular hard-stem feminine noun.

grammarFocus.construction: решишь (perfective future) + accusative эту проблему
grammarFocus.note: The perfective future решишь (of решить, 'to solve, once') takes the demonstrative эту (feminine) agreeing with проблему ('problem').

options.ru: Ты сможешь разобраться с этой проблемой?
options.note: смочь ('to be able') plus разобраться с ('to deal with') is an alternative.
получиться ('to work out') focuses on the outcome.

paraphrases.simplest: Решишь проблему? — dropping эту gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: The key pair: a single resolution (решить) vs. habitual problem-solving (решать).

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: история is a regular soft-stem feminine noun (the -ия type).

grammarFocus.construction: imperative расскажи (perfective) + dative мне + accusative историю
grammarFocus.note: Расскажи, the imperative of the perfective рассказать ('to tell'), takes both dative мне ('to me') and the accusative историю ('story,' feminine).

options.note: поделиться ('to share') plus the instrumental историей is an alternative.
что случилось ('what happened') is a more specific request.

paraphrases.simplest: Расскажи историю. — dropping мне gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: The basic pattern for 'tell someone something' in a command.

skeleton.note: plural genitive, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: сила is a regular hard-stem feminine noun; its genitive plural is сил.

grammarFocus.construction: у меня нет (negated possession) + genitive сил
grammarFocus.note: У меня нет ('I don't have') is the negated-possession construction; the object сил (genitive plural of сила, 'strength') takes the genitive.

options.note: без сил ('without strength') is more colloquial.
измотан ('exhausted,' short-form adjective) is an alternative.

paraphrases.simplest: Нет сил. — dropping у меня gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: An extremely common construction for 'X doesn't have Y,' a frequent fixed phrase for exhaustion.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, prepositional, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: сторона is a feminine noun with an irregular stress shift.

replies.ru: Я знал, что могу на тебя рассчитывать.
replies.gloss: I knew I could count on you.

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + на + prepositional (твоей стороне, on your side)
grammarFocus.note: На ('on') requires the prepositional, here твоей стороне (prepositional of твоя сторона). No быть appears in the present tense.

options.note: поддерживать ('to support') is a verb-based phrasing.
с тобой ('with you') is a shorter expression of solidarity.

paraphrases.simplest: Я с тобой. — swapping на твоей стороне for с тобой gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.pattern: на + prepositional (on someone's side, fixed phrase)
takeaway.note: A fixed prepositional construction for 'being on someone's side.'

skeleton.note: masculine noun, accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: конец is a masculine noun with a fleeting vowel (конец→конца).

grammarFocus.construction: видишь (imperfective) + accusative конец улицы
grammarFocus.note: Видеть ('to see') is imperfective; конец (masculine, accusative same as nominative) plus улицы (genitive of улица) forms a compound object.

options.note: где кончается ('where it ends') is a subordinate-clause alternative.
видно ('visible,' impersonal) is another construction.

paraphrases.simplest: Видишь конец улицы? — dropping ты gives a more natural colloquial form.

takeaway.note: The basic pattern where a following genitive expresses 'part of' something, as in конец улицы ('the end of the street').

skeleton.note: neuter noun, accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: начало is a regular hard-stem neuter noun.

grammarFocus.construction: помнишь (imperfective) + accusative начало фильма
grammarFocus.note: Помнить ('to remember') is imperfective; начало (neuter, accusative same as nominative) plus фильма (genitive of фильм) forms a compound object.

options.note: как начинался ('how it began') is a subordinate-clause alternative.

options.ru: Что было в начале фильма, помнишь?
options.note: что было ('what happened') is another phrasing.

paraphrases.simplest: Помнишь начало? — dropping фильма gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: The basic pattern where a following genitive expresses 'part of' something, as in начало фильма ('the beginning of the film').

skeleton.note: feminine noun, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: часть is a soft-stem feminine noun.

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + nominative часть моей жизни
grammarFocus.note: No быть appears; ты (nominative) and часть моей жизни ('part of my life,' nominative) are linked directly. Моей (feminine) agrees with жизни (genitive of жизнь).

options.note: важен ('important,' short-form adjective) is more direct.

options.ru: Без тебя моя жизнь не та.
options.note: без тебя ('without you') is more emotional.

paraphrases.simplest: Ты важная часть жизни. — dropping моей gives a slightly different but close phrasing.

takeaway.note: Basic rule: present-tense 'to be' statements omit быть — applies to figurative statements too.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, prepositional, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: случай is a regular hard-stem masculine noun; в этом случае is a fixed phrase meaning "in that case".

grammarFocus.construction: в этом случае ('in this case,' fixed phrase) + zero copula + adjective согласен
grammarFocus.note: В этом случае ('in this case') uses the prepositional of случай ('case'). Согласен ('agree,' a short-form adjective) agrees with the subject's gender.

options.note: при таких обстоятельствах ('under such circumstances') is more written.
тогда ('then') is a shorter phrasing.

paraphrases.simplest: Тогда согласен. — swapping в этом случае for тогда gives a shorter phrasing.

takeaway.note: The basic short-form adjective for 'to agree,' agreeing with gender/number.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, instrumental, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: каким образом is a fixed instrumental phrase meaning "in what way".

grammarFocus.construction: каким образом ('in what way,' fixed phrase) + знаешь (imperfective)
grammarFocus.note: Каким образом ('how, in what manner') uses the instrumental of образ ('manner'), a slightly more formal synonym of как ('how').

options.note: как ('how,' more colloquial) is a shorter alternative.

grammarFocus.note: Russian uses no verb for 'to be' in the present tense; the adjective itself is the predicate and agrees with the subject in gender and number.

variations.note: the feminine высокая when addressing a woman
the plural высокие for several people

options.note: такой ('so') adds an exclamatory note
using the noun рост ('height') with у + genitive, more matter-of-fact

paraphrases.simplest: Ты высокий. — dropping очень gives the basic form.

takeaway.pattern: subject + adjective (zero copula, agreeing in gender and number)
takeaway.note: No linking verb in the present tense, and the predicate adjective must agree with the subject.

skeleton.note: adjective, masculine, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: горячий means "hot".

replies.gloss: Let's wait for it to cool.

grammarFocus.construction: пьём (irregular 1st person plural of пить) + accusative (горячий кофе, an indeclinable masculine noun) + the adverb осторожно
grammarFocus.note: пить is irregular, with the stem пь- (пью, пьёшь, пьёт…). кофе never changes form but counts as masculine, hence горячий.

variations.note: with a 1st-person singular subject the verb is пью
with чай, a normally declining masculine noun

options.ru: Мы пьём кофе осторожно, он горячий.
options.note: splitting the reason into a following clause
swapping in потихоньку ('slowly, gingerly,' colloquial)

paraphrases.simplest: Мы пьём горячий кофе. — dropping осторожно gives the basic form.

takeaway.pattern: The irregular conjugation of пить (пью, пьёшь, пьёт, пьём, пьёте, пьют)
takeaway.note: A top-frequency irregular verb — and note that кофе is an indeclinable masculine noun.

skeleton.note: adjective, feminine accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: чистый means "clean".

grammarFocus.construction: ищем (imperfective present, 1st person plural of искать) + accusative (чистую комнату, feminine -ую/-у)
grammarFocus.note: искать takes the stem ищ-. A feminine noun phrase in the accusative pairs the adjective ending -ую with the noun ending -у.

variations.note: with a 1st-person singular subject the verb is ищу
the accusative plural чистые комнаты (inanimate, so identical to the nominative)

options.note: using the нужен construction (dative + нужна + nominative)
using снять ('to rent') + infinitive to state the purpose

paraphrases.simplest: Нам нужна чистая комната. — at a hotel or rental desk this gets the point across fastest.

takeaway.pattern: искать + accusative ('to look for,' no preposition)
takeaway.note: 'To look for' takes a direct accusative, and this is the place to lock in the feminine accusative -ую/-у.

skeleton.note: adjective, plural, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: грязный means "dirty".

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + nominative plural (грязные руки, plural adjective agreement)
grammarFocus.note: руки is nominative plural, so the adjective is plural грязные too (the singular is рука, and the stress shifts in the plural).

variations.note: for one hand only, the feminine singular грязная рука

options.note: using the possessive мои plus a zero-copula adjective predicate
using надо + infinitive — 'I need to wash my hands'

paraphrases.simplest: У меня грязные руки. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: у + genitive + plural adjective + nominative plural (bodily state)
takeaway.note: Paired body parts like руки, ноги, глаза are used in the plural, with plural adjective agreement.

skeleton.note: adjective, masculine, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: спокойный means "calm".

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + a noun-phrase predicate (спокойный человек, nominative) + the intensifier очень
grammarFocus.note: When the predicate is a noun phrase, it also stands in the nominative; the instrumental is used in the past and future or in writing.

variations.note: addressing a woman, both adjective and noun go feminine
addressing several people, the predicate phrase takes the nominative plural

options.note: dropping человек and leaving just the adjective as predicate
using the noun характер ('temperament') with у + genitive

paraphrases.simplest: Ты очень спокойный. — dropping человек is shortest and sounds natural.

takeaway.pattern: subject + adjective + noun (nominative predicate, zero copula)
takeaway.note: No linking verb in the present, and the predicate noun phrase stays nominative. In the past it shifts: Он был спокойным человеком (instrumental).

skeleton.note: adjective, masculine genitive=accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: бывший means "former/ex-".

grammarFocus.construction: обсуждать (imperfective) + accusative (бывшего начальника — animate masculine, accusative = genitive) with the negation не
grammarFocus.note: Animate masculine nouns take the genitive form in the accusative, which is why the adjective appears as бывшего.

variations.note: with a female boss the accusative is бывшую начальницу
animate plurals also take accusative = genitive: бывших коллег

options.ru: Мы не говорим о бывшем начальнике.
options.note: using говорить о + prepositional, which changes the case government

options.ru: Мы не сплетничаем о бывшем начальнике.
options.note: using сплетничать ('to gossip'), more colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Мы не говорим о нём. — with a pronoun this is the most compact version in speech.

takeaway.note: With a person as object, both adjective and noun take genitive endings — contrast with the inanimate бывший план.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular feminine pronoun, subject, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: она is the 3rd-person singular pronoun referring to a female person or feminine noun.

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the possessive моя + a noun predicate (сестра, nominative)
grammarFocus.note: The possessive мой agrees with the noun's gender; the feminine сестра takes моя.

variations.note: for a male, pronoun, possessive and noun all go masculine
in the plural: мои сёстры (nominative plural)

options.note: using это — the standard formula for introducing someone
using the dative мне, rather colloquial and explanatory

paraphrases.simplest: Это моя сестра. — when introducing someone this is the natural choice.

takeaway.pattern: Это + possessive + noun (the formula for introducing people)
takeaway.note: Introductions start with это rather than она. A good place to lock in possessive agreement (мой/моя/моё/мои).

skeleton.note: short-form adjective, masculine, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: the short form виноват of виноватый is used in predicate position.

replies.ru: Я знаю, что это не ты.

grammarFocus.construction: the short-form adjective виноват (predicate only) with the negation не
grammarFocus.note: In predicate position виноватый appears as the short form виноват/виновата/виноваты; the long form modifies a noun ('a guilty man').

variations.note: a female speaker uses the feminine виновата

options.note: using the noun вина ('fault')
a set colloquial phrase: 'I have nothing to do with it'

paraphrases.simplest: Я не виноват. — the simplest and strongest way to deny blame.

takeaway.pattern: Short-form adjectives as predicates (виноват / виновата / виноваты)
takeaway.note: виноват, рад, готов and должен appear only in the short form as predicates, and must agree in gender and number.

skeleton.note: готовить, 3rd person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: готовить is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of cooking.

grammarFocus.construction: готовит (imperfective present, 3rd person singular) + accusative (суп — inanimate masculine, accusative = nominative)
grammarFocus.note: The imperfective present covers both 'is cooking now' and 'always cooks.' The perfective is приготовить.

variations.note: the perfective past gives the result: she has finished making the soup
with a plural subject the verb is готовят

options.note: варить ('to boil') names the cooking method more precisely
dropping the object and adding a location, conversational

paraphrases.simplest: Мама готовит суп. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: варить for boiling, жарить for frying — but готовить is the all-purpose cover term.

skeleton.note: петь, 2nd person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: петь is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of singing.

grammarFocus.construction: поёшь (irregular 2nd person singular of петь) + the adverb of manner хорошо
grammarFocus.note: петь takes the stem по- (пою, поёшь, поёт, поём, поёте, поют). The imperfective present also conveys ability — 'you sing well.'

variations.note: formal or plural address uses поёте
the past tense makes it a one-off judgement: 'you sang well yesterday'

options.note: using the noun голос ('voice') with у + genitive
swapping in здорово ('great,' colloquial) for a more casual compliment

paraphrases.simplest: Ты хорошо поёшь. — the simplest version of this compliment.

takeaway.pattern: imperfective present + хорошо (to be good at something)
takeaway.note: Ability is expressed with the imperfective present — the same frame as Ты хорошо говоришь по-русски.

skeleton.note: учиться, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: учиться is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of studying/learning.

replies.gloss: How long have you been studying?

grammarFocus.construction: учиться (reflexive, imperfective) + infinitive (говорить) + the adverb по-русски
grammarFocus.note: учиться takes an infinitive in the sense 'to practise until you can do it.' по-русски is an adverb and needs no preposition.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is учимся
with a different language (по- + adjective stem + -ски)

options.note: using изучать + accusative, implying more systematic study
using заниматься + instrumental

paraphrases.simplest: Я учу русский язык. — for 'I'm learning Russian' this is the shortest version that lands.

takeaway.pattern: учиться + infinitive (to learn how to do something)
takeaway.note: Keep three apart: учиться (reflexive, to study), учить + accusative (to memorise), изучать + accusative (to study formally).

skeleton.note: повторять, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: повторять is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of reviewing/repeating.

grammarFocus.construction: повторяю (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + accusative plural (новые слова — inanimate, accusative = nominative)
grammarFocus.note: Inanimate plural noun phrases are identical in the accusative and nominative, so новые is unchanged. The perfective is повторить.

variations.note: in the singular: новое слово (neuter singular accusative)
with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is повторяем

options.note: using учить ('to memorise')
using закреплять ('to consolidate'), textbook phrasing

paraphrases.simplest: Я повторяю слова. — dropping новые is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: повторять / повторить + accusative (to review, to repeat)
takeaway.note: повторять слова is the set phrase for vocabulary review; Повторите, пожалуйста ('say that again') comes from the same verb.

keyPoint: изменить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of changing.

replies.gloss: I know, it's hard to accept.

grammarFocus.construction: можешь (2nd person singular of мочь) + perfective infinitive (изменить) + accusative (это) with the negation не
grammarFocus.note: мочь + infinitive expresses (in)ability. A perfective infinitive here says the result cannot be achieved.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses можете
the past tense gives 'I couldn't change it' (мог/могла)

options.note: an impersonal construction with just the infinitive: 'it can't be changed now'
a set colloquial phrase: 'there's nothing to be done'

paraphrases.simplest: Это не изменить. — the bare infinitive construction is shortest and sounds most resigned.

takeaway.pattern: не могу / не можешь + perfective infinitive (can't manage to do it)
takeaway.note: мочь always takes an infinitive. A perfective infinitive denies the result; an imperfective one denies the activity itself.

keyPoint: создать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of creating.

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + perfective infinitive (создать) + accusative (сайт)
grammarFocus.note: хотеть + infinitive expresses a wish. The perfective infinitive makes it result-oriented: to get the site built.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is хотим

options.note: using сделать ('to make'), more colloquial
using нужно + infinitive ('I need to')

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу сделать сайт. — in everyday speech сделать is the simpler, more natural verb.

takeaway.pattern: хочу + perfective infinitive (I want to get X done)
takeaway.note: хотеть takes an infinitive; perfective means 'want to accomplish,' imperfective 'want to be doing.'

keyPoint: отдать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of handing over/returning.

grammarFocus.construction: отдай (perfective imperative) + dative (мне) + accusative (телефон)
grammarFocus.note: отдать means to hand something back to its rightful owner, taking the recipient in the dative and the object in the accusative.

variations.note: with a different dative: 'give it to her'

options.note: дать drops the 'give back' sense and just means 'let me have it'
вернуть ('to return') makes the demand for the return explicit

paraphrases.simplest: Дай мне телефон. — simplest if you just want it handed over; use Отдай/Верни to demand it back.

takeaway.pattern: отдать + dative (person) + accusative (thing) = to hand back
takeaway.note: Learn the trio with examples: дать (to give), отдать (to give back, to hand over), вернуть (to return).

keyPoint: передать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of handing over/conveying.

grammarFocus.construction: передай (perfective imperative) + accusative (это) + dative (отцу)
grammarFocus.note: передать is to pass something along or relay a message; the recipient is dative, and note the fleeting vowel: отец → отцу.

options.note: using отдать ('to hand over')
for a verbal message, сказать ('to say') is the natural choice

paraphrases.simplest: Передай это отцу. — works for both objects and messages, so it's the most versatile.

takeaway.note: передать привет ('say hi for me') is extremely common, and передай соль ('pass the salt') belongs at any table.

keyPoint: принять is perfective, denoting a single completed act of accepting/deciding.

grammarFocus.construction: the short-form adjective должен (obligation) + perfective infinitive (принять) + accusative (решение)
grammarFocus.note: должен occurs only as a predicate and agrees with the subject (должен/должна/должны). принять решение ('to make a decision') is a fixed phrase.

options.note: using dative + нужно + infinitive, somewhat softer
using придётся ('you'll have to') + решить

paraphrases.simplest: Тебе нужно решить. — short and less pushy, which makes it easy to use in conversation.

takeaway.pattern: должен / должна / должны + infinitive (must do something)
takeaway.note: The key obligation pattern: a short-form adjective agreeing with the subject, as opposed to нужно, which takes the dative.

skeleton.note: принимать, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: принимать, the imperfective of принять, expresses the ongoing act of taking medicine.

grammarFocus.construction: принимаю (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + accusative (лекарство) + the time adverb утром (from the instrumental)
grammarFocus.note: утром, днём, вечером and ночью are frozen instrumental forms used adverbially, with no preposition.

variations.note: with a different time (вечером = in the evening)
with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is принимаем

options.note: using пить ('to drink'), more colloquial
по утрам ('every morning') stresses the habit

paraphrases.simplest: Я пью лекарство утром. — пить sounds more natural in everyday speech.

takeaway.pattern: утром / днём / вечером / ночью (time adverbs from the instrumental)
takeaway.note: These express 'in the morning' etc. with no preposition; pair them with the iterative по утрам ('every morning').

keyPoint: отказаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of refusing.

grammarFocus.construction: могу (1st person singular of мочь) + reflexive perfective infinitive (отказаться) with the negation не
grammarFocus.note: отказаться is reflexive and marks what you refuse with от + genitive (отказаться от предложения); here the object is left out.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is можем

variations.ru: Я не могу отказаться от этого предложения.
variations.note: spelling out what is refused with от + genitive

options.note: using the set phrase 'I have no choice'
using придётся ('I'll have to') + согласиться

paraphrases.simplest: Я не могу отказаться. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: отказаться от + genitive (to refuse or give up something)
takeaway.note: An essential reflexive verb that also means 'to quit': отказаться от курения ('to give up smoking').

keyPoint: согласиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of agreeing.

grammarFocus.construction: the short-form adjective готов ('ready') + perfective infinitive (согласиться)
grammarFocus.note: готов is predicate-only and agrees with the subject (готов/готова/готовы); it takes an infinitive directly: 'ready to do X.'

options.note: with мочь it becomes a neutral 'I can agree'
adding пожалуй ('I suppose') makes the agreement tentative

paraphrases.simplest: Я согласен. — for plain agreement this one short-form adjective is simplest.

takeaway.pattern: готов / готова / готовы + infinitive (ready to do something)
takeaway.note: Frequent in negotiation. согласиться marks what you agree to with с + instrumental (a person) or на + accusative (terms).

keyPoint: доказать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of proving.

grammarFocus.construction: можешь (2nd person singular of мочь) + perfective infinitive (доказать) + accusative (это), marked as a question by intonation
grammarFocus.note: Russian questions keep the statement word order; intonation (and the question mark in writing) does the work.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses можете
adding an instrumental of means: 'prove it with facts'

options.note: using the noun доказательства ('evidence') with у + genitive
asking with the instrumental interrogative чем ('with what')

paraphrases.simplest: У тебя есть доказательства? — in conversation this is the most direct and natural way to ask.

takeaway.pattern: Questions keep statement word order and rely on intonation
takeaway.note: No auxiliary inversion as in English. If there is a question word, it goes first (Чем ты докажешь?).

skeleton.note: обещать, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: обещать was originally biaspectual; in modern usage пообещать serves as its perfective.

grammarFocus.construction: обещаю (present, 1st person singular) + dative (тебе) + infinitive (помочь)
grammarFocus.note: обещать takes the person promised in the dative and the content as an infinitive. помочь also governs the dative, so 'to help you' is помочь тебе.

variations.note: the dative вам for formal or plural address
with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is обещаем

options.note: обязательно ('definitely') + perfective future, focused on the action
using the set phrase дать слово ('to give one's word')

paraphrases.simplest: Я помогу, обещаю. — perfective future plus обещаю is what people actually say.

takeaway.note: помогать/помочь also takes the dative (помочь тебе) — using the accusative for the person helped is a frequent mistake.

keyPoint: простить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of forgiving.

grammarFocus.construction: можешь (2nd person singular of мочь) + perfective infinitive (простить) + accusative (меня)
grammarFocus.note: простить takes the person forgiven in the accusative (простить меня); to name the offence as well, use простить мне что (dative + accusative).

variations.note: formal or plural address uses можете

variations.ru: Ты можешь простить мне эту ошибку?
variations.note: dative + accusative: 'can you forgive me this mistake?'

options.note: apologising directly with the imperative
using извинить, a lighter apology

paraphrases.simplest: Прости меня. — when apologising, the imperative is the simplest and most natural.

takeaway.note: Three registers to keep straight: Прости (casual), Простите (polite), Извини(те) (light).

keyPoint: вспомнить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of recalling.

grammarFocus.construction: могу (1st person singular of мочь) + perfective infinitive (вспомнить) + accusative (имя, an irregular -мя neuter noun) with не
grammarFocus.note: имя inserts -ен- from the genitive onward, but its accusative is identical to the nominative: имя.

variations.ru: Я не могу вспомнить его имя.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is можем

options.note: using забыть ('to forget'), more direct
an idiom: 'the name flew out of my head'

paraphrases.simplest: Я забыл имя. — shortest and perfectly clear in conversation.

takeaway.pattern: вспомнить (to recall) / помнить (to remember) / забыть (to forget)
takeaway.note: вспомнить is the perfective moment of recall; помнить is the imperfective state of remembering. Learn all three together.

skeleton.note: past masculine, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: заметить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of noticing.

replies.gloss: I was here the whole time.

grammarFocus.construction: заметил (perfective past, masculine singular) + accusative (тебя) with the negation не
grammarFocus.note: заметить is the perfective of noticing something at a moment. The object stays accusative even under negation here (a genitive object is also possible).

variations.note: a female speaker uses не заметила
with a 1st-person plural subject, не заметили

options.note: using видеть ('to see'), more general
with an apology — what people actually say

paraphrases.simplest: Я тебя не видел. — simplest way to say you didn't notice someone.

takeaway.note: замечать/заметить is noticing something that comes into view — distinct from понять ('to understand') and узнать ('to find out').

keyPoint: узнать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of finding out.

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + perfective infinitive (узнать) + accusative (правду, feminine -у)
grammarFocus.note: узнать is the perfective 'to find out, to learn.' The feminine правда takes the accusative правду.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is хотим

options.note: the imperfective знать makes it a state: 'I want to know'
using the imperative of рассказать, more direct

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу знать правду. — the version people use most often in conversation.

takeaway.pattern: узнать (to find out, perfective) / знать (to know, imperfective)
takeaway.note: узнать is learning something new; знать is holding the knowledge. New information vs. standing state.

keyPoint: предложить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of proposing.

grammarFocus.construction: можно (impersonal predicate) + perfective infinitive (предложить) + accusative (план)
grammarFocus.note: можно takes no subject and is followed by an infinitive to ask 'may I…?' — the standard way to request permission.

variations.note: adding the dative мне to name who is asking
with a different object: 'may I suggest a different plan?'

options.note: using the imperative of разрешить, noticeably more formal
using the noun предложение to open without asking permission

paraphrases.simplest: Можно предложить? — dropping the object makes it light enough for any meeting.

takeaway.note: The core permission pattern. Learn it with Можно мне…? and its negative counterpart Нельзя + infinitive.

skeleton.note: предлагать, 2nd person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: предлагать is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of proposing.

grammarFocus.construction: the interrogative pronoun что (accusative) + предлагаешь (imperfective present, 2nd person singular)
grammarFocus.note: The inanimate interrogative что is identical in the nominative and accusative; here it is the verb's object, placed first.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses предлагаете
the perfective future asks what you will propose, as a single act

options.note: using the noun предложения ('suggestions')
'what shall we do?' — more colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Что предлагаешь? — dropping ты is the most natural version in speech.

takeaway.pattern: Put the interrogative что (nominative = accusative) first
takeaway.note: Unlike animate кто (accusative/genitive кого), что shows no case distinction — the verb's government tells you which case it is.

skeleton.note: полагать, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: полагать is a stative imperfective verb meaning "to suppose".

grammarFocus.construction: полагаю (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + the adverb так
grammarFocus.note: полагать is a stative verb meaning 'to suppose,' rather formal in register; так полагаю is the set way to say 'I suppose so.'

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is полагаем
adding a что clause to state the content of the supposition

options.note: using думать — the most common, colloquial choice
using казаться + dative for a more tentative 'it seems so to me'

paraphrases.simplest: Я так думаю. — the simplest, most natural version in everyday speech.

takeaway.pattern: Я полагаю, что... / Я думаю, что... / Мне кажется, что...
takeaway.note: Three registers for stating an opinion: полагать is bookish, думать neutral, кажется the most tentative.

keyPoint: представить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of imagining/presenting.

grammarFocus.construction: можешь (2nd person singular of мочь) + perfective infinitive (представить) + accusative (это)
grammarFocus.note: In the sense 'to imagine,' представить often adds the reflexive dative себе — представить себе — though speech usually drops it.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses можете
the fuller version with себе (same meaning)

options.note: a single imperfective word meaning 'can you imagine? / you won't believe it' — very common in speech
using вообразить ('to picture'), slightly bookish

paraphrases.simplest: Представляешь? — one word is the simplest and most natural way to share surprise.

takeaway.note: Beyond the literal 'imagine,' it works as a conversational opener meaning 'listen to this.'

skeleton.note: представлять, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: представлять is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of representing/introducing.

grammarFocus.construction: представляю (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + accusative (нашу компанию — feminine, -ую/-ию)
grammarFocus.note: In the sense 'to represent,' представлять is imperfective and stative. A feminine noun phrase in the accusative pairs -ую with -ию (компания → компанию).

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is представляем
with a masculine noun (inanimate, so accusative = nominative)

options.note: из + genitive is the most common way to state where you're from
using работать в + prepositional

paraphrases.simplest: Я из этой компании. — shortest and most natural when introducing yourself.

takeaway.note: The standard business introduction. Careful: the perfective представить means 'to introduce' or 'to present,' a different sense.

skeleton.note: существовать, 3rd person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: существовать is imperfective, expressing the ongoing state of existing.

grammarFocus.construction: существует (imperfective present, 3rd person singular) with the nominative subject такой человек, marked as a question by intonation
grammarFocus.note: существовать is a stative imperfective ('to exist'). The demonstrative такой agrees in gender and number (такой/такая/такое/такие).

variations.note: with a feminine noun it becomes такая
in the plural both adjective and verb go plural

options.note: using бывать ('to happen to exist'), more colloquial
разве ('surely not') + есть adds a note of disbelief

paraphrases.simplest: Такие люди бывают? — in speech бывать sounds more natural here.

takeaway.pattern: такой / такая / такое / такие ('such a…', agreeing in gender and number)
takeaway.note: такой always agrees with its noun, and it is also the standard exclamation word: Такой красивый!

skeleton.note: past masculine, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: исчезнуть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of vanishing.

grammarFocus.construction: исчез (perfective past, masculine singular) + the adverb вдруг
grammarFocus.note: Most verbs in -нуть drop the -ну- in the past (исчезнуть → исчез, исчезла) — and the masculine form takes no -л at all.

variations.note: with a feminine subject, исчезла (the -л- reappears outside the masculine)

options.note: using пропасть ('to go missing'), more colloquial
не стало + genitive — 'he was suddenly gone,' also a euphemism for dying

paraphrases.simplest: Он вдруг пропал. — пропасть is what people actually say.

takeaway.pattern: The past tense of -нуть verbs (исчез / исчезла / исчезли)
takeaway.note: Same group as привыкнуть → привык and погибнуть → погиб: no -л in the masculine past.

skeleton.note: past masculine, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: появиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of appearing.

grammarFocus.construction: появился (reflexive perfective past, masculine singular) + the adverb вдруг
grammarFocus.note: появиться is reflexive; the -ся stays in the past: появился / появилась / появились.

options.note: using прийти ('to come'), more concrete
an idiom: 'he sprang up as if out of the ground'

paraphrases.simplest: Он вдруг пришёл. — when a person shows up, прийти is the natural verb.

takeaway.note: Learn the pair together. появляться is 'to keep appearing'; появиться is a single appearance.

keyPoint: подойти is perfective, denoting a single completed act of approaching.

grammarFocus.construction: подойди (perfective imperative) + ко + dative (мне)
grammarFocus.note: The preposition к becomes ко before awkward consonant clusters: ко мне, ко всем.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses подойдите
a different к + dative target (к stays as к)

options.note: идти + сюда ('come here') — the most colloquial option
adding пожалуйста to soften it

paraphrases.simplest: Иди сюда. — shortest and most natural with someone close to you.

takeaway.pattern: к + dative ('toward, over to') / ко мне (a phonetic variant)
takeaway.note: The к/ко choice is purely about pronunciation — memorise ко мне, ко всем, ко вторнику as units.

skeleton.note: подходить, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: подходить is imperfective, expressing the state of "suiting/fitting".

grammarFocus.construction: подхожу (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + dative (тебе)
grammarFocus.note: In the sense 'to suit, to be right for,' подходить takes the dative. In the physical sense 'to walk up to,' it takes к + dative.

variations.note: the dative вам for formal or plural address
with a thing as subject: 'does this job suit you?'

options.note: нравиться + dative turns it into a question about liking
adding как + nominative to name the role

paraphrases.simplest: Я тебе подхожу? — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: подходить + dative ('to suit, to be right for')
takeaway.note: Это мне подходит ('that works for me') is essential for arranging plans. Physical approach is подходить к + dative.

keyPoint: зайти is perfective, denoting a single completed act of dropping by.

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + perfective infinitive (зайти) + в + accusative (магазин)
grammarFocus.note: зайти is to drop in somewhere along the way; the destination takes в/на + accusative. The perfective infinitive makes it a single errand.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is хотим
к + dative makes it 'drop in on a friend'

options.note: надо + в + accusative with no verb at all — very common in speech
using заглянуть ('to pop in'), lighter

paraphrases.simplest: Мне надо в магазин. — dropping the verb makes it the shortest option.

takeaway.pattern: зайти в + accusative (into a place) / зайти к + dative (to a person)
takeaway.note: Places take в/на + accusative, people к + dative — the heart of how motion verbs work.

keyPoint: снять is perfective, denoting a single completed act of taking off [clothing].

grammarFocus.construction: можно (impersonal predicate) + perfective infinitive (снять) + accusative (пальто, an indeclinable neuter noun)
grammarFocus.note: пальто never changes form, so the accusative looks the same. снять is to take off something you're wearing.

variations.note: adding the dative мне to name who is asking
with a normally declining feminine noun the accusative is куртку

options.note: using мочь, slightly more direct
asking where to leave it — practical in someone's home

paraphrases.simplest: Можно снять пальто? — the natural set phrase when arriving somewhere.

takeaway.pattern: снять (to take off) ↔ надеть (to put on)
takeaway.note: Learn снять пальто and надеть пальто together. снять also means 'to rent' and 'to film' — a busy word.

keyPoint: снимать (here "to film/photograph") is imperfective, expressing an ongoing act.

grammarFocus.construction: нельзя (impersonal predicate of prohibition) + imperfective infinitive (снимать) + the adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: нельзя with an imperfective infinitive means 'it is forbidden'; with a perfective infinitive it means 'it is impossible.'

options.note: a noun plus the short passive participle запрещена — the wording you see on signs
a negative imperative (imperfective) stopping someone directly

paraphrases.simplest: Здесь нельзя снимать. — simplest for saying it out loud.

takeaway.note: Compare Здесь нельзя парковаться ('no parking') with Его нельзя найти ('he can't be found').

keyPoint: сесть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of sitting down.

grammarFocus.construction: можно (impersonal predicate) + perfective infinitive (сесть) + the adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: сесть is the perfective 'to sit down' (the act), while сидеть is 'to be sitting' (the state). Asking about a seat calls for сесть.

variations.note: adding the dative мне to name who is asking

options.note: 'is this seat free?' — by far the most common thing people actually say
asking from the other side, with занято ('taken')

paraphrases.simplest: Здесь свободно? — in a café or on a train this is overwhelmingly the natural question.

takeaway.pattern: сесть (to sit down, perfective) / сидеть (to be sitting, imperfective)
takeaway.note: Садитесь, пожалуйста ('do have a seat') is the polite imperfective imperative; Сядьте sounds like an order.

keyPoint: встать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of getting up.

grammarFocus.construction: the short-form adjective должен (obligation) + perfective infinitive (встать) + the adverb сейчас
grammarFocus.note: должен agrees with the subject (должен/должна/должны). встать is the perfective 'to get up, to stand up.'

options.note: dative + нужно + infinitive, softer
пора ('it's time to') + imperfective infinitive

paraphrases.simplest: Мне пора вставать. — the natural thing to say in the morning.

takeaway.pattern: должен + infinitive (must) / пора + infinitive (it's time to)
takeaway.note: должен expresses obligation, пора the right moment — and пора normally takes an imperfective infinitive.

keyPoint: вставать is imperfective, expressing habitual getting up.

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + the impersonal predicate трудно + imperfective infinitive (вставать) + the time adverb утром
grammarFocus.note: Impersonal predicates like трудно, легко and приятно take no subject; the person experiencing it goes in the dative. The habit calls for the imperfective вставать.

options.note: using с трудом ('with difficulty') plus a conjugated verb
using любить + infinitive to frame it as a preference

paraphrases.simplest: Мне трудно вставать утром. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: The core impersonal pattern — the same frame as Мне холодно ('I'm cold') and Мне интересно ('I find it interesting').

keyPoint: бросить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of throwing.

grammarFocus.construction: брось (perfective imperative) + dative (мне) + accusative plural (ключи — inanimate, accusative = nominative)
grammarFocus.note: брось ends in a soft sign. The inanimate plural ключи is identical in the accusative and nominative.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses бросьте

options.note: using кинуть ('to chuck'), more colloquial
using передать ('to pass') if you'd rather it not be thrown

paraphrases.simplest: Кинь ключи. — shortest and most colloquial among friends.

takeaway.note: бросить also means 'to quit' — бросить курить ('to quit smoking'). Context changes everything.

keyPoint: поймать (here "to catch/hail a taxi") is perfective, denoting a single completed act.

replies.gloss: Let's book one through an app.

grammarFocus.construction: помоги (perfective imperative) + dative (мне) + perfective infinitive (поймать) + accusative (такси, indeclinable)
grammarFocus.note: помочь takes the person helped in the dative. такси never changes form, and поймать такси is the set phrase for hailing a cab.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses помогите

options.note: using вызвать ('to call, to order') — the phrasing for a phone or app
turning it into a question about where to find one

paraphrases.simplest: Вызови такси, пожалуйста. — with ride apps the norm, вызвать is the practical choice.

takeaway.note: помочь is one of the key dative verbs. Also keep поймать такси (to hail) apart from вызвать такси (to order).

keyPoint: стрелять is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of shooting.

replies.gloss: I don't want to hurt you.

grammarFocus.construction: negative imperative: не + imperfective imperative (стреляй) + в + accusative (меня)
grammarFocus.note: Negative commands take the imperfective. стрелять marks the target with в + accusative (стрелять в цель).

variations.note: formal or plural address uses не стреляйте
with a different в + accusative target

options.note: не надо + infinitive — 'there's no need to shoot'
a concrete instruction: 'lower your weapon'

paraphrases.simplest: Не стреляй! — dropping в меня is shortest and most urgent.

takeaway.note: The target takes в + accusative, the weapon из + genitive (стрелять из пистолета) — note how the prepositions divide the work.

skeleton.note: защищать, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: защищать is imperfective, expressing the ongoing act of protecting.

replies.gloss: What are you protecting them from?

grammarFocus.construction: защищаю (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + accusative (свою семью) with the reflexive possessive свой
grammarFocus.note: свой means 'belonging to the subject,' and works with any person — Я защищаю свою семью. The feminine accusative is свою.

variations.note: with a 3rd-person subject свою means his own family (его would suggest someone else's)
with a plural accusative: свои права

options.note: using заботиться о + prepositional ('to take care of')
using стоять за + accusative ('to stand by')

paraphrases.simplest: Я защищаю свою семью. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: свой (the subject's own) vs его / её (someone else's)
takeaway.note: Он любит свою жену ('his own wife') and Он любит его жену ('someone else's wife') differ completely. свой is essential grammar.

keyPoint: защитить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of protecting.

replies.ru: Спасибо, я чувствую себя в безопасности.
Я могу сам о себе позаботиться.
replies.gloss: I can take care of myself.

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + perfective infinitive (защитить) + accusative (тебя)
grammarFocus.note: The perfective защитить is result-oriented — to get you protected; the imperfective защищать is ongoing defence.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is хотим
with the formal or plural accusative вас

options.note: the negated оставить — 'I won't abandon you'
'I'll be right here' — warmer and more natural

paraphrases.simplest: Я буду рядом. — in real conversation this carries more weight and sounds more natural.

takeaway.pattern: защищать (ongoing defence) / защитить (to get someone protected)
takeaway.note: Aspect separates sustained protection from a single rescue, and хочу + perfective is result-oriented.

keyPoint: победить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of winning.

grammarFocus.construction: the short-form adjective должны (obligation, plural) + perfective infinitive (победить)
grammarFocus.note: победить is defective: it has no 1st person singular future. 'I will win' has to be Я одержу победу or Я смогу победить.

variations.note: with a masculine singular subject, должен

options.note: using выиграть ('to win' a game or a prize)
using the noun победа with dative + нужна

paraphrases.simplest: Мы должны выиграть. — in sports выиграть is the more usual verb.

takeaway.pattern: победить has no 1st person singular future (a defective verb)
takeaway.note: There is no *я побежду. Use Я смогу победить or Я одержу победу instead.

keyPoint: спасти is perfective, denoting a single completed act of saving/rescuing.

replies.ru: Да, что бы это ни стоило.

grammarFocus.construction: хочешь (2nd person singular of хотеть) + accusative (меня, placed before the verb) + perfective infinitive (спасти)
grammarFocus.note: Russian word order is flexible, and pronoun objects usually sit before the verb: Ты хочешь меня спасти?

variations.note: formal or plural address uses хотите
the object after the infinitive — same meaning, slightly different emphasis

options.note: помочь + dative — gentler and more realistic
жалко + dative + accusative — 'do you feel sorry for me?'

paraphrases.simplest: Ты хочешь мне помочь? — the natural choice in an ordinary situation.

takeaway.pattern: Pronoun objects naturally go before the verb
takeaway.note: Я тебя люблю, Он меня не понимает — pronouns before the verb, while noun objects normally follow it.

skeleton.note: болеть, 1st person singular present, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: болеть is imperfective, expressing the ongoing state of being/getting sick.

grammarFocus.construction: болею (imperfective present, 1st person singular, in the sense 'to be ill') + the frequency adverb редко
grammarFocus.note: болеть has two patterns: for a person being ill it conjugates болею, болеешь; for an aching body part only the 3rd person болит / болят is used.

variations.note: with a different frequency adverb and a season

options.note: using почти не ('hardly ever')
using the noun здоровье ('health') with у + genitive

paraphrases.simplest: Я редко болею. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: болеть ('a person is ill': болею) / болеть ('a body part aches': болит)
takeaway.note: One infinitive, two conjugation patterns. Learn Я болею alongside У меня болит голова.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: брат is a masculine noun with an irregular plural, братья.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + есть + nominative (брат)
grammarFocus.note: брат has an irregular nominative plural братья (genitive plural братьев) — one of the nouns with a collective -ья plural.

variations.note: the negation takes нет + genitive, so it becomes брата

options.note: adding старший ('older') for specifics
saying it indirectly: 'I'm not an only child'

paraphrases.simplest: У меня есть брат. — the basic way to talk about family.

takeaway.pattern: брат → братья (irregular plural); negation is нет + genitive
takeaway.note: Same -ья group as сын → сыновья and друг → друзья. Lock in У меня нет брата (genitive) at the same time.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: сестра is a feminine noun with an irregular plural, сёстры.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + есть + nominative (сестра)
grammarFocus.note: сестра is irregular: nominative plural сёстры, genitive plural сестёр — involving both the ё shift and a fleeting vowel.

variations.note: the feminine две governs the genitive singular сестры

options.note: adding младшая ('younger') for specifics
using the collective numeral двое: 'there are two of us in the family'

paraphrases.simplest: У меня есть сестра. — the basic way to talk about family.

takeaway.note: With numerals the form shifts: две сестры (genitive singular), пять сестёр (genitive plural). Learn it with the numeral rules.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: бабушка is a regular hard-stem feminine noun.

grammarFocus.construction: the possessive моя + nominative (бабушка) + живёт (imperfective present, 3rd person singular) + the adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: жить is irregular, with a в in the stem: живу, живёшь, живёт, живём, живёте, живут.

variations.note: in the plural both possessive and verb go plural
the past tense takes the feminine жила

options.note: в + prepositional names the actual dwelling
a zero-copula sentence, closer to 'my grandmother is here'

paraphrases.simplest: Бабушка живёт здесь. — dropping the possessive is shortest; context supplies it.

takeaway.pattern: The irregular conjugation of жить (живу, живёшь, живёт, живём, живёте, живут)
takeaway.note: A top-frequency verb. Where you live takes в/на + prepositional: жить в Москве.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, dative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: дядя grammatically ends in -я but is masculine.

grammarFocus.construction: звоню (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + dative (дяде) + the frequency adverb часто
grammarFocus.note: звонить takes the person called in the dative. дядя ends in -я but is masculine, declining like a feminine noun (дядя → дяде).

variations.note: with a female relative in the dative (тётя → тёте)
with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is звоним

options.note: using разговаривать с + instrumental, which changes the case government

options.ru: Мы с дядей часто на связи.
options.note: using the colloquial на связи ('in touch')

paraphrases.simplest: Я часто звоню дяде. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: звонить + dative ('to call someone'); дядя is masculine but declines like a feminine noun
takeaway.note: Using the accusative here is a common error (*звонить дядю). Learn it alongside мужчина, папа and дядя.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, genitive, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: день рождения is the fixed compound phrase for "birthday".

replies.gloss: How do you usually celebrate it?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative (свой день рождения) — the set phrase день + genitive рождения
grammarFocus.note: день рождения is a noun plus a genitive, fixed in place. Only день declines (masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative); the genitive рождения never changes.

variations.note: with a different possessor (свой can only refer back to the subject)
in the plural only день pluralises: дни рождения

options.note: using нравиться + dative

options.ru: Я всегда жду свой день рождения.
options.note: using ждать ('to look forward to') for a note of anticipation

paraphrases.simplest: Я люблю свой день рождения. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: день рождения (noun + genitive, the genitive part invariable)
takeaway.note: С днём рождения! ('happy birthday' — instrumental after с) is the phrase you'll use most. Only день ever changes case.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: свадьба is a regular hard-stem feminine noun.

replies.gloss: How many guests are you planning?

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + accusative (большую свадьбу, feminine -ую/-у)
grammarFocus.note: A feminine noun phrase in the accusative pairs the adjective ending -ую with the noun ending -у: the hard-stem свадьба becomes свадьбу.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is хотим
with a different adjective (маленькую also ends in -ую)

options.note: using мечтать о + prepositional ('to dream of'), which changes the case
using хочется + dative for a softer wish

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу большую свадьбу. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: большую свадьбу, чистую комнату, новую машину — learn the pairing as one shape.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: вечеринка is a regular hard-stem feminine noun.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (нас) + nominative (вечеринка) + the adverb сегодня — an есть-less existence/plan construction
grammarFocus.note: у + genitive covers not only possession but 'we've got something on.' Dropping есть turns it into a statement about plans or circumstances.

options.note: using устраивать + accusative ('to throw a party')
using собираться ('to gather') to say guests are coming

paraphrases.simplest: У нас сегодня вечеринка. — the natural way to announce a plan.

takeaway.pattern: У + genitive + time adverb + nominative ('we have X on')
takeaway.note: The same frame as У меня завтра экзамен ('I have an exam tomorrow') and У нас в пятницу встреча.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: встреча is a regular hard-stem feminine noun.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + nominative (важная встреча, feminine singular agreement) — an есть-less construction for plans
grammarFocus.note: The adjective важная is feminine singular nominative, agreeing with встреча. Dropping есть shifts the focus to what kind of engagement it is.

variations.note: in the plural both adjective and noun take nominative plural

options.note: нужно + на + accusative with no verb — colloquial
adding занят (a short-form adjective) when turning something down

paraphrases.simplest: У меня встреча. — dropping важная is shortest and enough as an excuse.

takeaway.pattern: У меня встреча ('I have a meeting') + an adjective to describe it
takeaway.note: The standard way to decline on grounds of a prior engagement. У меня дела ('I have things to do') works the same way.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural accusative, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: разговор is a regular hard-stem masculine noun.

replies.gloss: What do you usually talk about?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative plural (долгие разговоры — inanimate, accusative = nominative)
grammarFocus.note: Inanimate plural noun phrases are identical in the accusative and nominative. любить + accusative plural states a general liking.

variations.note: in the singular (masculine inanimate, so accusative = nominative)
with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is любим

options.note: using нравиться + dative — the conversations become the subject, so the verb goes plural
using the adverb долго with an infinitive

paraphrases.simplest: Я люблю долгие разговоры. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: любить + accusative plural (to like X in general)
takeaway.note: General preferences take the accusative plural. Note that with animates the accusative equals the genitive: Я люблю собак, not собаки.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, genitive, this sentence's target word

keyPoint: звонок is a masculine noun with a fleeting vowel (звонок→звонка).

grammarFocus.construction: ждать + genitive (твоего звонка — note the fleeting vowel: звонок → звонка)
grammarFocus.note: ждать normally takes the genitive for what you're waiting on. звонок has a fleeting о, which drops from the genitive onward.

variations.note: with a different possessor (её is invariable)
with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is ждём

options.note: using a когда clause with a verb instead
splitting it into an imperative plus a short clause — conversational

paraphrases.simplest: Жду твоего звонка. — dropping я is the standard sign-off in letters and messages.

the negated imperative of шуметь ('don't make noise')

keyPoint: легко means "easily".

grammarFocus.note: Russian adverbs are normally formed by replacing the adjective ending with -о: серьёзный → серьёзно, быстрый → быстро.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is говорим
adding the accusative это: 'I mean this seriously'

options.note: the negated шутить ('I'm not joking') — the most colloquial option
using the short-form adjective серьёзен as predicate

paraphrases.simplest: Я не шучу. — the version that really lands when you need to be taken seriously.

takeaway.note: This is how adverbs are built — and note it coincides with the impersonal predicate form (Мне трудно).

keyPoint: правильно means "correctly".

grammarFocus.construction: говоришь (imperfective present, 2nd person singular) + the adverb of manner правильно, placed after the verb
