grammarFocus.construction: оставь (perfective imperative) + accusative (меня) + в + prepositional (покое) — a set phrase
grammarFocus.note: оставить в покое means 'to leave someone alone.' покой takes the prepositional покое.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses оставьте
with a different accusative: 'leave him alone'

options.note: the negated imperative of трогать ('don't touch, don't bother me')
дать + infinitive: 'let me have some time alone' — gentler

paraphrases.simplest: Оставь меня в покое. — the set phrase, and the most forceful.

takeaway.pattern: оставить в покое ('to leave alone' — a fixed phrase)
takeaway.note: Learn оставить + accusative + в покое as a unit; Дай мне побыть одному is the gentler alternative.

keyPoint: Извинить is perfective, meaning "to forgive" (pairs with извинять).

grammarFocus.construction: извини (perfective imperative) + accusative (меня) + за + accusative (это)
grammarFocus.note: извинить takes the person forgiven in the accusative and the reason in за + accusative — the same frame as простить.

variations.note: formal or plural apology uses извините
dropping меня and keeping just the reason — the most natural version

options.note: with простить, a weightier apology
dative + жаль to express regret

paraphrases.simplest: Извини за это. — dropping меня is the natural version.

takeaway.note: Извини за опоздание, за беспокойство, за задержку — за + accusative is the standard way to name the reason.

keyPoint: Подождать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "waiting a bit" (pairs with ждать).

grammarFocus.construction: подожди (perfective imperative) + accusative (меня) + accusative of duration (одну минуту)
grammarFocus.note: подождать can take its object in either the accusative or genitive. Duration goes in the accusative with no preposition (одну минуту, два часа).

variations.note: formal or plural request uses подождите
with немного ('a bit'), leaving the time vague

options.note: dropping the verb — the most compact set phrase
'I'll be quick, hang on' — split into two clauses

paraphrases.simplest: Одну минуту! — enough on its own for 'just a moment.'

takeaway.pattern: Duration takes the bare accusative (одну минуту / два часа / всю неделю)
takeaway.note: Duration is accusative; clock time is в + accusative (в два часа). That split is the core of time expressions.

keyPoint: Подумать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "thinking it over a bit" (pairs with думать).

grammarFocus.construction: дай (perfective imperative) + dative (мне) + perfective infinitive (подумать) + the adverb немного
grammarFocus.note: дать + dative + infinitive means 'let someone do something.' подумать, with по-, means thinking for a little while.

variations.note: formal or polite request uses дайте
inserting the accusative время for a fuller phrasing

options.note: using dative + нужно + infinitive
perfective future: 'I'll think and let you know'

paraphrases.simplest: Дай подумать. — dropping мне still works.

takeaway.pattern: дать + dative + infinitive ('let someone do something')
takeaway.note: Дай мне сказать ('let me speak'), Дайте пройти ('let me through'). A core way to ask permission.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Чувствовать is imperfective, meaning "to feel" (pairs with почувствовать).

grammarFocus.construction: чувствовать себя (a fixed phrase with the reflexive себя) + the adverb плохо
grammarFocus.note: To describe how you feel, use чувствовать себя plus an adverb — плохо, хорошо, нормально — never an adjective.

variations.note: with a 3rd-person singular subject (себя is invariable)

options.note: dative + the impersonal плохо — the shortest version
using the perfective past of заболеть ('I've fallen ill')

paraphrases.simplest: Мне плохо. — the shortest way to say you feel unwell.

takeaway.pattern: чувствовать себя + adverb / Мне плохо (the dative construction)
takeaway.note: Как вы себя чувствуете? ('how are you feeling?') is essential at a doctor's. себя is always there.

keyPoint: Черта is a feminine noun meaning "trait, feature."

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (тебя) + nominative (интересная черта, feminine agreement)
grammarFocus.note: черта ('trait, line') is a hard-stem feminine noun. In this есть-less possessive the adjective интересная agrees as feminine singular nominative.

variations.note: in the plural both adjective and noun take nominative plural

options.note: adding характера ('of character') to be specific
using по-своему ('in your own way') to appraise the whole person

paraphrases.simplest: У тебя интересная черта. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: черта means both 'trait' and 'line' — черты лица ('facial features') is another frequent use.

keyPoint: Дома is a location adverb meaning "at home," distinct from the directional домой ("homeward").

grammarFocus.construction: nominative (мама) + the time adverb сейчас + the locative adverb дома, with zero copula
grammarFocus.note: No verb for 'to be' in the present. The notable point is that дома means 'at home' and takes no preposition.

variations.note: in the past the copula была appears
another location takes на + prepositional (дома is the adverbial exception)

options.note: dropping сейчас — the shortest version
stating it negatively: 'she hasn't gone anywhere'

paraphrases.simplest: Мама дома. — shortest and most natural.

takeaway.pattern: дома is an adverb and takes no preposition
takeaway.note: Different from в доме ('inside the building'). Learn дома / домой / из дома as a set.

keyPoint: Три is a numeral; with the numbers 2-4 the noun takes the singular genitive form.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + the numeral три + genitive singular (брата)
grammarFocus.note: два, три and четыре put the following noun in the genitive singular (три брата); five and up take the genitive plural (пять братьев).

variations.note: with five and up, the genitive plural братьев
feminine nouns follow the same rule: the genitive singular сестры

options.note: using the collective numeral четверо for family size
conveying it without a number

paraphrases.simplest: У меня три брата. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: 2-4 + genitive singular / 5 and up + genitive plural
takeaway.note: два брата vs пять братьев, две сестры vs пять сестёр — the single most important numeral rule in Russian.

keyPoint: Вещь is a feminine noun meaning "thing," with soft-stem declension endings.

grammarFocus.construction: купила (perfective past, feminine singular) + accusative (полезную вещь — a feminine noun in -ь, accusative = nominative)
grammarFocus.note: Feminine nouns in -ь like вещь don't change in the accusative; only the adjective ending полезную marks the case.

variations.note: in the plural: полезные вещи (inanimate, so accusative = nominative)
with a normally declining feminine noun, the noun changes too

options.note: что-то with a neuter adjective, vaguer
using the noun покупка ('purchase') to appraise it

paraphrases.simplest: Она купила полезную вещь. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: Feminine nouns in -ь (вещь, речь, мысль) have accusative = nominative
takeaway.note: Only the adjective's -ую reveals the accusative — a decisive clue when reading.

keyPoint: Отлично is the adverbial form of the adjective отличный, meaning "excellently."

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb отлично (from отличный via -о) + готовит (imperfective present, 3rd person singular) + accusative (кофе, indeclinable)
grammarFocus.note: отлично means 'excellently' and appraises skill. The imperfective present is what expresses 'is good at.'

variations.note: with хорошо ('well'), a more measured compliment

options.note: using у + genitive with an adjective
a dash construction with the superlative лучший

paraphrases.simplest: Она отлично готовит кофе. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: imperfective present + adverb ('to be good at')
takeaway.note: Она отлично готовит, Ты хорошо поёшь — ability always takes the imperfective present.

keyPoint: Похоже functions as a parenthetical meaning "apparently, it seems."

grammarFocus.construction: the parenthetical похоже (set off by commas) + perfective past (пришла) + the adverb уже
grammarFocus.note: похоже means 'it looks like' and is more evidence-based than кажется. It takes commas on both sides.

variations.note: with a masculine subject the past is пришёл
with the parenthetical at the front

options.note: with кажется, more subjective
with видимо ('apparently'), somewhat more formal

paraphrases.simplest: Похоже, она уже пришла. — the natural way to hedge this guess.

takeaway.note: похоже rests on evidence, кажется on impression, видимо leans to the written register.

skeleton.note: future 3rd person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Прийтись is a perfective impersonal verb meaning "to be forced to" (pairs with приходиться).

replies.gloss: Why does she have to leave?

grammarFocus.construction: знает + a colon introducing the content + dative (ей) + придётся (impersonal perfective future) + infinitive (уйти)
grammarFocus.note: придётся means 'will have to' and is impersonal: the person goes in the dative and there is no subject at all.

variations.note: the past пришлось: 'she had to leave'

options.ru: Она знает, что ей нужно уйти.
options.note: a что clause with нужно, more neutral

options.ru: У неё нет выбора — надо уходить.
options.note: spelling out the reason: 'she has no choice'

paraphrases.simplest: Ей придётся уйти. — dropping the main clause is shortest and clearest.

takeaway.note: Мне придётся работать. The past is пришлось; present necessity is нужно or надо.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Выглядеть is a stative verb of appearance with no perfective counterpart.

grammarFocus.construction: выглядишь (imperfective present, 2nd person singular) + the adverb хорошо + the time adverb сегодня
grammarFocus.note: выглядеть means 'to look' and takes an adverb (выглядеть хорошо) — in contrast to казаться, which takes the instrumental.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses выглядите
the exception: a state adjective takes the instrumental (уставшим)

options.note: with отлично, a stronger compliment
using идти + dative ('this look suits you')

paraphrases.simplest: Хорошо выглядишь! — dropping subject and time makes the best compliment.

takeaway.pattern: выглядеть + adverb ('to look') / казаться + instrumental ('to seem')
takeaway.note: выглядеть хорошо vs казаться умным — different case government, so learn them together.

keyPoint: Послушать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "listening a bit" (pairs with слушать).

grammarFocus.construction: послушай (perfective imperative) + accusative (эту песню, feminine -у)
grammarFocus.note: послушать, with по-, means giving something a listen. The feminine песня has the accusative песню.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses послушайте
the imperfective слушай makes it 'keep listening to it'

options.note: with включить ('put it on'), more concrete
услышать + надо: 'you have to hear this'

paraphrases.simplest: Послушай эту песню. — the natural way to recommend it.

takeaway.pattern: послушать (to give a listen) / слушать (to listen on)
takeaway.note: Послушай! ('listen a moment') also opens conversations. The prefix по- gives it that 'just once' sense.

keyPoint: Прямо is an adverb meaning "straight, directly."

replies.gloss: What do you want to say?

grammarFocus.construction: смотри (imperfective imperative) + the emphatic adverb прямо + на + accusative (меня)
grammarFocus.note: смотреть marks what you look at with на + accusative. прямо ('straight') sharpens the direction.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses смотрите
with в + accusative: 'look straight in the eye'

options.note: the perfective посмотри: 'take a look at me'
the negated отводить глаза ('don't look away')

paraphrases.simplest: Смотри на меня. — dropping прямо is shortest.

takeaway.note: Note the two patterns: смотреть на картину ('look at a picture') but смотреть телевизор ('watch television,' direct accusative).

keyPoint: Давайте is the formal/plural form of давай, meaning "let's."

grammarFocus.construction: the hortative particle давайте + perfective future 1st plural (поговорим) + об + prepositional (этом)
grammarFocus.note: давайте plus a perfective 1st plural is the polite 'let's.' поговорить marks its topic with о/об + prepositional, and о becomes об before a vowel.

variations.note: with someone close, the singular давай
обсудить takes a direct accusative, so о disappears

options.note: using dative + надо + infinitive
можно + infinitive — a more tentative opener

paraphrases.simplest: Давайте поговорим. — dropping об этом is shortest.

takeaway.note: давай for friends, давайте for politeness or plural. Note too that поговорить takes о + prepositional while обсудить takes the accusative.

keyPoint: Несколько is a quantity determiner meaning "a few," combined with the genitive plural.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + the quantifier несколько + genitive plural (вопросов)
grammarFocus.note: несколько ('several') governs the genitive plural, as do много, мало and сколько.

variations.note: with a different noun (genitive plural идей)

options.note: using пара ('a couple') + genitive to ask permission
the conditional with кое-что, more polite

paraphrases.simplest: У меня несколько вопросов. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: несколько / много / мало / сколько + genitive plural
takeaway.note: Quantifiers always take the genitive: несколько вопросов, много людей, сколько денег (genitive singular for uncountables).

keyPoint: Ага is a colloquial interjection of affirmation/agreement.

grammarFocus.construction: the affirmative interjection Ага (set off by a comma) + the time adverb теперь + perfective past (понял)
grammarFocus.note: Ага is a colloquial 'ah, I see.' теперь means 'now, at this point' and implies a change from before, unlike сейчас.

options.note: dropping the interjection — the standard version
a set phrase: 'so that's it!'

paraphrases.simplest: Теперь понятно. — the natural way to signal you've got it.

takeaway.pattern: теперь ('now, as of now') / сейчас ('right now')
takeaway.note: теперь contrasts with before; сейчас is the point in time. Теперь я понял is the classic use.

keyPoint: Добрый is an adjective meaning "kind."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the intensifier очень + adjective + noun predicate (добрый человек, nominative)
grammarFocus.note: A noun-phrase predicate stays in the nominative. добрый agrees with человек as masculine singular nominative.

variations.note: addressing a woman, both adjective and noun go feminine
for several people, the nominative plural добрые люди

options.note: dropping человек and leaving the adjective as predicate
using сердце ('heart') with у + genitive, more lyrical

paraphrases.simplest: Ты очень добрый. — dropping человек is the most natural.

takeaway.note: The standard way to appraise someone. In the past it shifts: Ты был добрым человеком (instrumental).

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word

keyPoint: "Как тебя зовут" literally means "what do they call you," a fixed expression using звать to ask someone's name.

grammarFocus.construction: the interrogative как + accusative (тебя) + зовут (3rd person plural, used impersonally) — the formula for asking a name
grammarFocus.note: Literally 'how do they call you.' The subjectless 3rd plural зовут is the standard way to ask someone's name.

variations.note: the accusative вас for formal or plural address

options.note: the imperative of представиться — formal
just the noun имя — short but blunt

paraphrases.simplest: Как тебя зовут? — the standard, natural way to ask.

takeaway.pattern: Как тебя / вас зовут? ('what's your name?') / Меня зовут… ('my name is…')
takeaway.note: The answer uses the same impersonal frame: Меня зовут Анна (accusative + зовут). Я Анна works too.

keyPoint: Должно is an impersonal predicate meaning "should" or "must be."

grammarFocus.construction: считает + a что clause + the impersonal predicate должно (neuter short form) + perfective infinitive (получиться)
grammarFocus.note: должно получиться means 'it should work out.' It is impersonal — no subject, and должно is fixed in the neuter.

variations.note: making всё the subject with a perfective future — more natural

options.note: using думать with выйти ('to work out')
using the short-form уверена with в + prepositional

paraphrases.simplest: Она думает, что получится. — what people actually say.

takeaway.pattern: должно получиться ('it should work out' — impersonal)
takeaway.note: должен/должна/должно/должны agree with a subject, but impersonally it's always neuter должно. Должно быть ('it must be') works the same way.

keyPoint: Уверен is the short form of уверенный, used in predicate position to mean "certain, sure."

grammarFocus.construction: the short-form adjective уверен (predicate) + в + prepositional (этом), with question intonation
grammarFocus.note: уверен is predicate-only and agrees in gender and number (уверен/уверена/уверены). What you're sure of takes в + prepositional.

options.note: using точно with знать, more colloquial
'is that definite?' — the shortest check

paraphrases.simplest: Ты уверен? — dropping в этом is shortest.

takeaway.note: Я уверен в себе ('I'm confident'), Я не уверен ('I'm not sure'). Don't forget the short-form agreement.

keyPoint: Ребята is a colloquial plural noun meaning "guys, folks."

grammarFocus.construction: позвала (perfective past, feminine singular) + accusative (ребят — animate plural, accusative = genitive) + на + accusative (ужин)
grammarFocus.note: ребята is a plural noun for 'the guys, everyone'; being animate, its accusative is ребят. What you invite someone to takes на + accusative.

variations.note: with a masculine subject the past is позвал

options.note: using пригласить ('to invite'), more formal
using для + genitive ('for the guys')

paraphrases.simplest: Она позвала ребят на ужин. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: позвать / пригласить + accusative + на + accusative ('to invite to')
takeaway.note: позвать is colloquial, приглашать formal. And note the animate plural accusative = genitive (ребят, друзей).

keyPoint: Жаль is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's a pity, I'm sorry."

grammarFocus.construction: direct speech + dative (мне) + the impersonal predicate жаль — 'I'm sorry'
grammarFocus.note: жаль takes no subject; the person feeling it goes in the dative. It shares a root with жалеть but exists only as a predicate.

variations.note: adding очень — the most natural version

options.note: using извиниться to report it indirectly
with Простите, a more direct apology

paraphrases.simplest: Мне жаль. — two words for 'I'm sorry.'

takeaway.pattern: dative + жаль ('I'm sorry, it's a shame')
takeaway.note: Мне жаль ('I'm sorry'), Мне жаль его ('I feel sorry for him' — accusative). Also the phrase for condolences.

keyPoint: Туда is an adverb of direction meaning "to there."

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + the directional adverb туда + infinitive (идти) with не
grammarFocus.note: туда means 'to there' (direction), paired with там ('there,' location). The negated не хочу denies the intention.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject, не хотим
with the locative там: 'I don't want to stay there'

options.note: хочется + dative — softer
offering an alternative with лучше

paraphrases.simplest: Я не хочу туда. — the infinitive can be dropped.

takeaway.note: идти туда vs быть там — direction and position take different adverbs.

keyPoint: Действительно is a confirming adverb meaning "really, actually."

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb действительно ('really') + the adverb так + думаешь (imperfective present, 2nd person singular), with question intonation
grammarFocus.note: действительно means 'really, in fact' and in a question it sharpens surprise. так means 'that way, so.'

variations.note: formal or plural address uses думаете

options.note: using серьёзно — the shortest expression of surprise
неужели ('surely not') conveys stronger disbelief

paraphrases.simplest: Ты серьёзно? — two words carry both surprise and the question.

takeaway.note: действительно is the most formal, правда colloquial, неужели the most incredulous.

skeleton.note: future 3rd person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Хватит is the future form of the perfective хватить, used as a fixed phrase meaning "enough, stop."

grammarFocus.construction: direct speech + the impersonal predicate Хватит + imperfective infinitive (спорить) — 'that's enough of…'
grammarFocus.note: Хватит is the 3rd singular of хватить used impersonally; it takes an infinitive to call a stop, and can also take a genitive (Хватит разговоров).

variations.note: with the genitive plural споров: 'enough arguing'

options.note: using the imperative of перестать — more standard
Довольно ('enough') as a one-word set phrase

paraphrases.simplest: Хватит! — one word for 'that's enough.'

takeaway.pattern: Хватит + imperfective infinitive or genitive ('enough of…')
takeaway.note: Хватит болтать ('stop chattering'), Хватит с меня ('I've had enough'). Impersonal, so no subject.

keyPoint: Использовать is a biaspectual verb meaning "to use."

replies.gloss: What do you need it for?

grammarFocus.construction: можно (impersonal predicate) + the biaspectual infinitive использовать + accusative (твой телефон)
grammarFocus.note: использовать is biaspectual — one form for both aspects. It takes the accusative, in contrast to пользоваться, which takes the instrumental.

variations.note: adding the dative мне to name who's asking
воспользоваться takes the instrumental and sounds more polite

options.note: using с + genitive ('call from your phone'), more specific
дать + accusative — the most colloquial request

paraphrases.simplest: Можно твой телефон? — dropping the verb is shortest and natural.

takeaway.pattern: использовать + accusative vs пользоваться + instrumental (both 'to use')
takeaway.note: The key case contrast: использовать возможность vs пользоваться телефоном.

skeleton.note: future 1st person plural, the target word

keyPoint: Поехать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "setting off" by vehicle (pairs with ехать).

grammarFocus.construction: the hortative particle давай + perfective future 1st plural (поедем) + на + accusative (море)
grammarFocus.note: поехать is travelling by vehicle. 'To the sea' is на море (на + accusative) — never в море.

variations.note: with a destination that takes в + accusative

options.note: the past поехали works colloquially as 'let's go!'
как насчёт + genitive ('how about…?') — a tentative suggestion

paraphrases.simplest: Поехали на море! — the most colloquial way to propose it.

takeaway.pattern: на море / на дачу (destinations taking на + accusative)
takeaway.note: на море and на работу take на; в Москву and в деревню take в. Each destination fixes its own preposition.

keyPoint: Больший is the comparative form of большой, meaning "greater."

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + the long-form comparative adjective больший + nominative (опыт)
grammarFocus.note: больший is the long-form comparative of большой and can modify a noun directly (больший опыт); as a predicate you use больше.

variations.note: the predicative comparative больше with the genitive опыта — the usual version

options.note: the one-word comparative of опытный

options.ru: У меня больше опыта, чем у него.
options.note: чем у + genitive to name the comparison

paraphrases.simplest: У меня больше опыта. — the predicative comparative plus genitive is the natural choice.

takeaway.pattern: Long-form comparatives (больший, лучший) modify nouns; short forms (больше, лучше) are predicates
takeaway.note: больший опыт vs опыта больше — and note that больше governs the genitive.

keyPoint: Отсюда is an adverb of direction meaning "from here."

grammarFocus.construction: the imperfective imperative уходи + the adverb of origin отсюда + the emphatic сейчас же
grammarFocus.note: отсюда means 'from here' and completes the trio with сюда ('to here') and здесь ('here'). сейчас же means 'right this instant.'

variations.note: formal or plural address uses уходите

options.note: the perfective уйди with немедленно — more final
using оставить — a polite way to ask someone to go

paraphrases.simplest: Уходи! — one word is forceful enough.

takeaway.note: A three-way adverb set. там / туда / оттуда works the same way.

keyPoint: Произойти is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "happening" (pairs with происходить).

grammarFocus.construction: знает + a что clause (indirect question) + произошло (perfective past, neuter singular)
grammarFocus.note: произойти ('to happen') takes inanimate subjects, and the neuter past произошло is the standard way to say what happened.

options.note: using быть в курсе ('to be in the know')
using известно + dative ('she knows it all')

paraphrases.simplest: Она знает, что случилось. — случилось is more natural in speech.

takeaway.note: произойти is written and journalistic, случиться colloquial. Both take inanimate subjects — never a person.

keyPoint: Единственный is an adjective meaning "only, sole."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the possessive моя + the adjective единственная + the noun predicate любовь (a feminine noun in -ь)
grammarFocus.note: любовь is a feminine -ь noun, so its modifiers моя единственная are feminine singular nominative.

variations.note: with a different noun (надежда — 'hope,' also feminine)
with a masculine noun the modifiers go masculine

options.note: using любить with только + accusative — more direct

options.ru: Кроме тебя, у меня никого нет.
options.note: using кроме + genitive ('apart from you') — more heartfelt

paraphrases.simplest: Я люблю только тебя. — the more direct way to say it.

takeaway.note: единственный друг, единственная любовь, единственное желание — and note любовь is a feminine -ь noun.

keyPoint: Верно is the adverbial form of the adjective верный, meaning "correctly."

grammarFocus.construction: сделал (perfective past, masculine singular) + accusative (всё) + the adverb of manner верно
grammarFocus.note: верно means 'correctly,' near-synonymous with правильно. всё is neuter singular, identical in the accusative and nominative.

variations.note: addressing a woman, the past is сделала
with правильно, the more common word

options.note: with правильно — the standard compliment
adding Молодец ('well done') for warmth

paraphrases.simplest: Всё верно. — two words for 'that's all correct.'

takeaway.note: Всё верно is also the set way to confirm what someone just said — 'that's right.'

keyPoint: Раньше is a time adverb meaning "before, previously."

replies.gloss: What did you like to read?

grammarFocus.construction: the time adverb раньше ('formerly') + the quantity adverb много + читал (imperfective past, masculine singular)
grammarFocus.note: раньше implies a contrast with now, and therefore always pairs with the imperfective past — the standard way to describe a changed habit.

options.note: spelling out the contrast with больше, чем сейчас
pinning the period down with в детстве ('as a child')

paraphrases.simplest: Раньше я много читал. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: раньше carries 'but not now' with it, and as a rule doesn't go with perfectives.

keyPoint: Оба is a numeral meaning "both," used with masculine/neuter nouns (its feminine form is обе).

replies.gloss: That's something we have in common.
What coffee do you two like?

grammarFocus.construction: the quantitative pronoun оба (masculine/neuter) in the nominative (мы оба) + любим (imperfective present, 1st person plural) + accusative (кофе)
grammarFocus.note: оба is for masculine and neuter, обе for feminine. мы оба is a pair including a male; мы обе is two women.

options.ru: Мы с ним оба любим кофе.
options.note: мы с ним ('he and I') spells out who's meant

options.ru: И я, и он любим кофе.
options.note: using и…, и… ('both… and…')

paraphrases.simplest: Мы оба любим кофе. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: оба брата, обе сестры — like the numerals up to four, they take the genitive singular.

keyPoint: Господь is a religious masculine noun meaning "the Lord."

grammarFocus.construction: nominative (Господь, an irregular masculine noun) + accusative (всё) + видит (imperfective present, 3rd person singular)
grammarFocus.note: Господь ('the Lord') has the irregular stem Господа from the genitive onward, and the vocative Господи also serves as an exclamation.

variations.note: with Бог ('God'), the more everyday wording
the vocative Господи in an exclamation or prayer

options.note: using ничто with от + genitive — more literary
a secular version: 'the truth always comes out'

paraphrases.simplest: Бог всё видит. — the more common and accessible wording.

takeaway.note: Господи! is extremely common as an everyday 'good heavens' — the religious force has largely faded.

keyPoint: Более is an adverb forming the analytic comparative, meaning "more."

grammarFocus.construction: the compound comparative более + the adverb уверенно + отвечает (imperfective present, 3rd person singular)
grammarFocus.note: более plus the base form makes a compound comparative, used where a simple comparative is awkward or the register calls for it. уверенно means 'confidently.'

variations.note: with the simple comparative увереннее, more colloquial

options.note: using the noun уверенность with с + instrumental — formal
framing it as a change with стать + infinitive and смелее

paraphrases.simplest: Она отвечает увереннее. — the simple comparative is more natural in speech.

takeaway.note: Speech prefers simple comparatives (быстрее, лучше); более suits formal registers and words with no simple form.

keyPoint: Итак is a connective adverb meaning "so, well then," marking a conclusion or start.

grammarFocus.construction: the connective parenthetical Итак (set off by a comma) + perfective future 1st plural (начнём, a hortative) + the adverb наконец
grammarFocus.note: Итак means 'so, right then' and moves the discourse forward. The perfective 1st plural начнём serves as 'let's begin.'

variations.note: dropping наконец — the most compact version
with Что ж ('well then'), more colloquial

options.note: давайте + perfective 1st plural — the standard invitation
the 1st plural of приступить — compact and formal

paraphrases.simplest: Итак, начнём. — the natural way to open a meeting or lesson.

takeaway.note: Итак, начнём; Итак, подведём итоги — the set way to mark a new stage in the discourse.

keyPoint: Ко is a euphonic variant of к ("to") used before certain consonant clusters.

grammarFocus.construction: the imperfective imperative приходи + ко + dative (мне) + the instrumental time adverb вечером
grammarFocus.note: The preposition к becomes ко before мне. приходить к + dative means coming to someone's place.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses приходите
with a different dative (к нам keeps plain к)

options.note: using заходить ('drop by') — a lighter invitation
using ждать + accusative ('I'll be expecting you')

paraphrases.simplest: Заходи вечером. — the most natural casual invitation.

takeaway.pattern: приходить к + dative (to a person) / ко мне (a phonetic variant)
takeaway.note: People take к + dative, places в/на + accusative. Memorise ко мне and ко всем as units.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Убийство is a neuter noun meaning "murder."

replies.ru: Какой фильм ей нравится больше всего?
replies.gloss: What movie does she like most?

grammarFocus.construction: любить + accusative plural (фильмы) + про + accusative (убийства, neuter plural)
grammarFocus.note: про is the colloquial 'about' and takes the accusative. убийство is a neuter -ство noun whose accusative plural is identical to the nominative: убийства.

variations.note: with о + prepositional, more written in register
with the noun детективы ('crime stories'), much shorter

options.note: using нравиться + dative with an adjective
using фанат + genitive ('a fan of'), colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Она любит детективы. — one genre word covers it, so this is shortest.

takeaway.note: фильм про войну (colloquial) vs фильм о войне (standard). про takes the accusative, о the prepositional.

skeleton.note: future 1st person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Забрать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "picking someone up" (pairs with забирать).

grammarFocus.construction: заберу (perfective future, 1st person singular of забрать) + accusative (тебя) + the instrumental time adverb вечером
grammarFocus.note: забрать is collecting someone or something and taking it away. The perfective future makes it a promise to pick you up. Its conjugation is irregular: заберу, заберёшь.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is заберём
adding из + genitive for where you're collecting from

options.note: using приехать за + instrumental ('come for you')
using встретить ('meet you')

paraphrases.simplest: Я заберу тебя вечером. — the natural way to promise a pickup.

takeaway.pattern: забрать + accusative (to collect and take away) / приехать за + instrumental
takeaway.note: забрать документы ('collect the documents'), забрать ребёнка из садика. за + instrumental is the set 'to fetch.'

keyPoint: Тело is a neuter noun meaning "body."

grammarFocus.construction: бережёт (imperfective present, 3rd person singular of беречь) + accusative (своё тело) with the reflexive possessive свой
grammarFocus.note: беречь means 'to take care of, to protect' and conjugates irregularly with a ж in the stem: берегу, бережёшь, бережёт.

variations.note: with a masculine subject (the verb form is unchanged)

options.note: using заботиться о + prepositional ('to look after')
using следить за + instrumental ('she looks after herself'), more colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Она следит за собой. — the most natural phrasing in conversation.

takeaway.pattern: беречь + accusative ('to take care of') / Береги себя! ('take care')
takeaway.note: Береги себя is the set parting phrase. The conjugation (берегу, бережёшь) is irregular — learn it whole.

skeleton.note: adjective, plural prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Далёкий is an adjective meaning "far, distant."

grammarFocus.construction: мечтает (imperfective present, 3rd person singular) + о + prepositional (далёких странах, prepositional plural)
grammarFocus.note: мечтать marks what you dream of with о + prepositional. The prepositional plural pairs the adjective ending -их with the noun ending -ах.

variations.note: in the singular: о далёкой стране (feminine singular prepositional)
with a plural subject and a different noun

options.note: using хотеть + infinitive, more concrete
using тянуть + accusative ('she's drawn to'), literary

paraphrases.simplest: Она мечтает о путешествиях. — the most natural and compact version.

takeaway.note: The prepositional plural ends -ых/-их plus -ах/-ях. мечтать о детях, о будущем follow the same pattern.

keyPoint: Момент is a masculine noun meaning "moment, instant."

grammarFocus.construction: подожди (perfective imperative) + accusative (один момент, the numeral один with a masculine noun)
grammarFocus.note: один agrees with the noun's gender, so the masculine момент takes один. Duration goes in the accusative with no preposition.

variations.note: formal or polite request uses подождите
with the feminine минута the numeral becomes одну

options.note: dropping the verb — the most compact set phrase
repeating сейчас to say 'coming right up,' colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Один момент. — dropping the verb is shortest and natural.

takeaway.pattern: один / одна / одно (один agrees in gender)
takeaway.note: один момент, одну минуту, одно слово. один is the one numeral that declines like an adjective.

keyPoint: Чёрт originally means "devil" but also functions as an interjection of surprise or frustration.

grammarFocus.construction: the curse-interjection Чёрт (set off by a comma) + the adverb опять + perfective past (опоздал)
grammarFocus.note: Чёрт is a mild 'damn.' опять means 'again' with a note of annoyance at the repetition.

options.note: with Блин (the mildest colloquial curse) and снова
using the negated успеть ('I didn't make it') with no curse at all

paraphrases.simplest: Опять опоздал. — dropping the curse and the subject is shortest.

takeaway.note: Он опять опоздал (irritation) vs Он снова пришёл (neutral). Блин is a softer curse than Чёрт.

keyPoint: Квартира is a feminine noun meaning "apartment, flat."

replies.gloss: How many rooms does it have?

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + the adjective маленькая + nominative (квартира) — an есть-less possessive
grammarFocus.note: Dropping есть turns it into a description of what kind of flat it is. маленькая agrees as feminine singular nominative with квартира.

variations.note: in the plural both adjective and noun take nominative plural
with a different possessor and adjective

options.note: using the possessive моя with a zero-copula adjective predicate
using жить в + prepositional, more concrete

paraphrases.simplest: У меня маленькая квартира. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: У + genitive + adjective + nominative (no есть — describing a possession)
takeaway.note: With есть the focus is the fact of having; without it, the quality. That contrast is the heart of the possessive.

keyPoint: Поздно is an adverb/impersonal predicate meaning "late."

replies.gloss: I don't want to sleep yet.

grammarFocus.construction: the impersonal predicate поздно + the adverb уже + imperfective imperative (иди) + infinitive (спать)
grammarFocus.note: поздно takes no subject. идти спать ('go to bed') is a motion verb plus infinitive and the most ordinary way to say it.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses идите

options.note: в + accusative with no verb — the shortest version
using the imperative of ложиться ('lie down')

paraphrases.simplest: Пора спать. — two words for 'time for bed.'

takeaway.pattern: идти спать ('go to bed') / пора спать ('time for bed')
takeaway.note: спать is the state of sleeping, идти спать the act of going to bed, ложиться спать specifically turning in.

skeleton.note: 3rd person feminine singular genitive, the target word

keyPoint: Неё is the genitive form of она; an н- is inserted after the preposition без ("without").

grammarFocus.construction: может (3rd person singular of мочь) + infinitive (жить) + без + genitive (неё, a 3rd-person pronoun with н-)
grammarFocus.note: After a preposition, 3rd-person pronouns take an н-: её → неё, его → него, их → них. без governs the genitive.

variations.ru: Он не может жить без него.
Они не могут жить без них.

options.note: using быть привязан к + dative ('she's deeply attached to her')

options.ru: Она не представляет жизни без неё.
options.note: using не представлять + genitive ('she can't imagine life without her')

paraphrases.simplest: Она не может без неё. — the infinitive жить can be dropped.

takeaway.pattern: 3rd-person pronouns take н- after a preposition (у неё / без него / с ними)
takeaway.note: её, его and их have no н- on their own, but always gain one after a preposition.

keyPoint: Господи is the vocative form of господь (Lord), used as an interjection of surprise or emotion.

replies.gloss: What tired you out so much?

grammarFocus.construction: the vocative-derived interjection Господи + the exclamatory как + perfective past (устал)
grammarFocus.note: Господи is the vocative of Господь, now an everyday 'good heavens.' как plus a predicate builds an exclamation: 'how tired I am!'

variations.note: with Боже (the vocative of Бог), near-identical in force

options.note: using так ('so') with no interjection
using без сил ('out of strength'), more concrete

paraphrases.simplest: Как я устал! — the exclamation carries fine without the interjection.

takeaway.note: Как красиво! ('how lovely'), Как жаль! ('what a shame'). Господи and Боже are now ordinary exclamations with little religious weight.

skeleton.note: future 1st person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Написать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "writing" (pairs with писать).

grammarFocus.construction: напишу (perfective future, 1st person singular of написать) + dative (тебе) + accusative (письмо)
grammarFocus.note: написать is the perfective 'to write (and finish).' The addressee goes in the dative and what you write in the accusative.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is напишем
dropping письмо: 'I'll write to you tomorrow'

options.note: dropping the object — the standard way to promise a message
using связаться с + instrumental ('I'll be in touch'), more formal

paraphrases.simplest: Я тебе напишу. — the natural way to say 'I'll message you.'

takeaway.note: Я тебе напишу is the set phrase for 'I'll text you.' Keep the писать/написать aspect pair in mind too.

keyPoint: Прошлый is an adjective meaning "past, last."

replies.gloss: Where did she go on vacation?

grammarFocus.construction: вспоминает (imperfective present, 3rd person singular) + accusative (прошлый отпуск, adjective plus masculine inanimate)
grammarFocus.note: прошлый means 'last, previous' — прошлый год, прошлая неделя. The noun is masculine inanimate, so the accusative equals the nominative.

variations.note: the perfective вспомнила marks a single moment of recall

options.note: using думать о + prepositional
using скучать по + dative ('she misses those days')

paraphrases.simplest: Она вспоминает прошлый отпуск. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: прошлый год / прошлая неделя / в прошлом месяце ('last…')
takeaway.note: прошлый is 'the previous one,' бывший 'former, ex-.' в прошлом году ('last year') uses the prepositional for time.

keyPoint: Вернуть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "returning" (pairs with возвращать).

replies.gloss: Okay, I'll give it back tomorrow.
How much do I owe you?

grammarFocus.construction: верни (perfective imperative of вернуть) + dative (мне) + accusative (мои деньги, a plural-only noun)
grammarFocus.note: вернуть is 'to give back,' with the recipient in the dative and the thing in the accusative. деньги exists only in the plural, so the possessive is plural too: мои.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses верните
with a feminine singular noun (мою книгу)

options.note: using отдать ('hand it over'), more colloquial
using долг ('the debt') to ask about timing instead

paraphrases.simplest: Верни мне деньги. — the possessive can be dropped.

takeaway.pattern: деньги is a plural-only noun (мои деньги / много денег)
takeaway.note: брюки, часы and ножницы behave the same way. The genitive денег turns up constantly with quantifiers.

skeleton.note: neuter noun, plural, the target word

keyPoint: Отношение is a neuter noun meaning "relationship," frequent in the plural form отношения.

replies.gloss: Have you known each other long?

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (нас) + the adjective хорошие + nominative plural (отношения)
grammarFocus.note: In the sense 'relationship,' отношения is used in the plural, with plural agreement хорошие. The singular отношение means 'attitude' or 'ratio.'

variations.note: with a different possessor and adjective

variations.ru: У нас хорошие отношения с соседями.
variations.note: adding с + instrumental for whom the relationship is with

options.note: using ладить ('to get on'), more colloquial
stating the relationship with a plain noun predicate

paraphrases.simplest: Мы хорошо ладим. — what people actually say.

takeaway.note: хорошие отношения vs хорошее отношение к работе — the number carries the meaning.

keyPoint: Поверить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "believing" (pairs with верить).

replies.ru: Что именно ты не можешь поверить?

grammarFocus.construction: могу (1st person singular of мочь) + perfective infinitive (поверить) with не
grammarFocus.note: поверить is the perfective 'to believe,' taking the person in the dative (поверить ему) and the content in в + accusative (поверить в это).

variations.ru: Я не могу поверить в это.
variations.note: в + accusative names what you can't believe
the dative names whom you can't believe

options.note: a one-word exclamation: 'unbelievable!'
a set colloquial 'no way!'

paraphrases.simplest: Не могу поверить! — dropping the subject is most natural as an exclamation.

takeaway.pattern: поверить + dative (to believe a person) / в + accusative (to believe in something)
takeaway.note: Я тебе верю ('I believe you') vs Я верю в тебя ('I believe in you') — an important contrast.

keyPoint: Хоть is an emphatic particle meaning "at least, even if."

grammarFocus.construction: позвони (perfective imperative) + dative (мне) + the particle хоть + the adverb иногда
grammarFocus.note: хоть means 'at least, if only' and marks a minimal request. позвонить takes the person called in the dative.

variations.note: formal or plural request uses позвоните

options.note: the imperfective imperative звони, framing it as a habit
the negated пропадать ('don't disappear on me'), warmer

paraphrases.simplest: Звони иногда. — two words for 'call me sometimes.'

takeaway.note: хоть иногда, хоть немного, хоть что-нибудь — the particle for a bare-minimum request.

keyPoint: Ужин is a masculine noun meaning "dinner."

grammarFocus.construction: приготовила (perfective past, feminine singular) + accusative (вкусный ужин — masculine inanimate, accusative = nominative)
grammarFocus.note: приготовить is the perfective of cooking something through. The masculine inanimate ужин is identical in the accusative and nominative.

variations.note: with a masculine subject the past is приготовил
with a feminine noun the accusative is вкусную еду

options.note: with the adverb вкусно modifying the cooking instead
using получиться ('it turned out well') to state the result

paraphrases.simplest: Она приготовила вкусный ужин. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: Three uses to keep apart: вкусный ужин, вкусно приготовить, and Вкусно! as an impersonal predicate.

keyPoint: Достаточно is a quantity adverb meaning "enough," combined with the genitive case.

replies.gloss: How much time do we have?

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (нас) + the quantity adverb достаточно + genitive (времени)
grammarFocus.note: достаточно ('enough') governs the genitive. время is an irregular -мя neuter noun whose genitive is времени.

variations.note: with the genitive денег of the plural-only деньги

options.note: using хватать ('to suffice') + genitive
describing it through the negated спешить ('we're in no rush')

paraphrases.simplest: Времени достаточно. — reordering gives the most natural short version.

takeaway.note: Also fix the irregular время / времени / временем. имя and время are the two -мя nouns to know.

keyPoint: Некоторый is a determiner meaning "some, a certain amount of."

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + нужно + accusative (некоторое время, with the indefinite adjective некоторый)
grammarFocus.note: некоторый means 'some, a certain amount of' and declines like an adjective. Its neuter singular accusative некоторое pairs with the accusative of duration.

variations.note: in the plural: нужны некоторые документы

options.note: with немного + the genitive времени, more colloquial
дать + dative + accusative — the shortest direct request

paraphrases.simplest: Дай мне время. — the most direct version when you're asking.

takeaway.pattern: The agreement of некоторый ('some, a certain')
takeaway.note: некоторое время ('a while'), некоторые люди ('some people'). некоторый declines like an adjective, unlike немного, which takes the genitive.

keyPoint: Попасть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting to" a place (pairs with попадать).

grammarFocus.construction: хочет (3rd person singular of хотеть) + perfective infinitive (попасть) + в + accusative (центр)
grammarFocus.note: попасть means managing to get somewhere, with в/на + accusative. It carries a sense of succeeding — getting a ticket, making it in time.

variations.note: with a destination taking на + accusative

options.note: using поехать ('to go by vehicle'), more neutral
dative + нужно + в + accusative with no verb — the most colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Ей нужно в центр. — dropping the verb is what people say.

takeaway.pattern: попасть в / на + accusative ('to manage to get to')
takeaway.note: попасть на поезд ('catch the train'), попасть в пробку ('get caught in traffic') — it also covers ending up somewhere unintentionally.

keyPoint: Провести is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "spending (time)" (pairs with проводить).

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + perfective infinitive (провести) + accusative (время) + с + instrumental (тобой)
grammarFocus.note: провести время ('to spend time') is a set phrase, with the company in с + instrumental. провести conjugates irregularly: проведу, проведёшь.

variations.ru: Мы хотим провести время с тобой.
variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is хотим

variations.ru: Я хочу провести вечер с тобой.
variations.note: with вечер ('the evening') as the object

options.note: using быть с + instrumental — more direct and heartfelt
давай + perfective 1st plural turns it into an invitation

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу быть с тобой. — the more natural way to say what you mean.

takeaway.pattern: провести время с + instrumental ('to spend time with')
takeaway.note: провести отпуск ('spend a holiday'), провести встречу ('hold a meeting') — провести is a busy verb.

keyPoint: Пять is the numeral "five"; the noun takes the genitive plural.

grammarFocus.construction: дай (perfective imperative) + dative (мне) + the numeral пять + genitive plural (минут)
grammarFocus.note: Numerals from five up take the genitive plural (пять минут); two to four take the genitive singular (две минуты).

variations.note: the feminine две takes the genitive singular минуты
formal or polite request uses дайте

options.note: dropping the verb — the most compact request

options.ru: Я буду готов через пять минут.
options.note: using через + accusative to say when you'll be ready

paraphrases.simplest: Пять минут! — the numeral alone gets the message across.

takeaway.pattern: пять минут (5+ with genitive plural) / две минуты (2-4 with genitive singular)
takeaway.note: одна минута / две минуты / пять минут — the three-way split is one of the most important rules in Russian.

keyPoint: Попросить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "asking" (pairs with просить).

replies.gloss: What do you want to ask?

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + accusative (тебя, before the verb) + perfective infinitive (попросить)
grammarFocus.note: попросить takes the person asked in the accusative, and what you're asking for in о + prepositional or an infinitive. Pronoun objects sit before the verb.

variations.note: with the formal or plural accusative вас

variations.ru: Я хочу попросить тебя об одном деле.
variations.note: об + prepositional names what you're asking about

options.note: using the noun просьба with к + dative — the set opener
можно + infinitive — the politest way to lead in

paraphrases.simplest: У меня к тебе просьба. — the natural way to raise a favour.

takeaway.note: Both просить помощи (genitive) and попросить о помощи (prepositional) work; the person is always accusative.

keyPoint: Рад is an adjective that exists only in the short form, meaning "glad."

replies.gloss: I'm glad to see you too.
It's been years since we've seen each other!

grammarFocus.construction: the short-form adjective рад (predicate) + infinitive (видеть) + accusative (тебя)
grammarFocus.note: рад is predicate-only and agrees in gender and number (рад/рада/рады). It takes an infinitive directly: 'glad to do something.'

options.note: adding как to heighten it into an exclamation
for a first meeting, 'pleased to meet you' is the right phrase

paraphrases.simplest: Рад тебя видеть! — dropping the subject makes the most natural greeting.

takeaway.note: Рад познакомиться ('pleased to meet you'), Рад помочь ('happy to help'). The short-form agreement is obligatory.

keyPoint: Второй is the ordinal numeral meaning "second."

grammarFocus.construction: живёт (imperfective present, 3rd person singular of жить) + на + prepositional (втором этаже, an ordinal in the prepositional)
grammarFocus.note: Floors take на + prepositional. The ordinal второй declines like an adjective, giving втором, and этаж has the prepositional этаже.

variations.note: with a different ordinal (the ground floor)

options.note: using the noun квартира with zero copula
using the comparative выше + genitive ('above us')

paraphrases.simplest: Она живёт на втором этаже. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: на + ordinal in the prepositional + этаже ('on the … floor')
takeaway.note: на первом / втором / третьем этаже. Floors take на, not в — learn the phrase as a unit.

keyPoint: Следовать is imperfective, meaning "to follow" (pairs with последовать).

grammarFocus.construction: следуй (imperfective imperative of следовать) + за + instrumental (мной)
grammarFocus.note: следовать за + instrumental means following behind someone; за with the instrumental marks 'after, behind.' In the sense 'to comply,' следовать takes the dative (следовать правилам).

variations.note: formal or plural address uses следуйте

options.note: using идти со + instrumental, softer and more colloquial
using идти за + instrumental — the everyday phrasing

paraphrases.simplest: Иди за мной. — the natural everyday version.

takeaway.pattern: следовать за + instrumental (to follow behind) / следовать + dative (to comply with)
takeaway.note: следовать за ним vs следовать правилам — the case changes with the sense.

keyPoint: Прислать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "sending" (pairs with присылать).

grammarFocus.construction: пришли (perfective imperative of прислать) + dative (мне) + accusative (фото, indeclinable neuter)
grammarFocus.note: прислать is sending something to where the speaker is. Note the imperative пришли looks identical to the past plural прислали — context decides. фото never declines.

variations.note: formal or polite request uses пришлите
with a different object: 'send me the link'

options.note: using отправить ('to send') — the most general wording
using скинуть ('to ping over'), younger colloquial speech

paraphrases.simplest: Скинь фото. — the most colloquial option in a messaging context.

takeaway.pattern: прислать (to send here) / отправить (to send off)
takeaway.note: прислать points toward the speaker, отправить away from them. Пришли мне vs Я отправлю тебе.

keyPoint: Родитель is a masculine noun meaning "parent"; its plural родители means "parents."

replies.gloss: Do you see each other often?

grammarFocus.construction: the possessive мои + nominative plural (родители) + живут (imperfective present, 3rd person plural) + the adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: родители ('parents') is used in the plural; the singular родитель means a single parent and sounds official. The possessive goes plural too: мои.

options.note: using с + instrumental ('I live with my parents')
using рядом ('nearby') with no verb

paraphrases.simplest: Мои родители живут здесь. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: родители, дети and люди are plural by default. The singular родитель belongs to official contexts.

skeleton.note: future 1st person plural, the target word

keyPoint: Встретиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "meeting" (pairs with встречаться).

grammarFocus.construction: the hortative particle давай + perfective future 1st plural (встретимся, with reciprocal -ся) + the adverb завтра
grammarFocus.note: The -ся in встретиться is reciprocal — 'meet each other.' давай plus a perfective 1st plural is the natural 'let's.'

variations.note: naming the time with в + accusative

options.note: using увидеться in the 1st plural as a question
как насчёт + genitive ('how about tomorrow?') — tentative

paraphrases.simplest: Давай встретимся завтра. — the natural way to fix a meeting.

takeaway.pattern: Давай встретимся ('let's meet') / встретиться с + instrumental
takeaway.note: Name the other person with с + instrumental; with a plural subject the reciprocal -ся makes that unnecessary.

keyPoint: Капитан is a masculine noun meaning "captain."

grammarFocus.construction: a nominative form of address (Капитан) + the interrogative что + dative (нам) + infinitive (делать) — an impersonal question
grammarFocus.note: что + dative + infinitive asks 'what are we to do?' There is no subject; the infinitive carries the question.

options.note: using указания ('orders') — military and formal
dropping the dative and adding дальше ('next')

paraphrases.simplest: Что делать? — two words for 'what should we do?'

takeaway.pattern: dative + infinitive ('what is one to do' — impersonal)
takeaway.note: Что мне делать?, Куда нам идти? — a key pattern using a bare infinitive with no subject.

keyPoint: Остальной is an adjective meaning "remaining, the rest of."

grammarFocus.construction: съела (perfective past, feminine singular) + accusative (остальной торт, adjective plus masculine inanimate)
grammarFocus.note: остальной means 'the rest of, the remaining' and declines like an adjective; in the plural остальные also works as a noun for 'the rest of them.'

variations.note: with a feminine noun the accusative is остальную пиццу
остальные used as a noun: 'the rest went home'

options.note: using доесть ('to finish eating') — shorter and more natural
using the clause что осталось ('what was left')

paraphrases.simplest: Она доела торт. — доесть does it in one word.

takeaway.note: в остальном ('as for the rest') and остальные used as a noun are both frequent.

skeleton.note: 1st person plural present, the target word

keyPoint: Встречаться is imperfective, meaning "to meet" (pairs with встретиться).

grammarFocus.construction: встречаемся (imperfective present, 1st person plural, with reciprocal -ся) + accusative of time (каждый день)
grammarFocus.note: встречаться means both 'to meet each other' and 'to be dating.' каждый день ('every day') takes the bare accusative for frequency.

variations.ru: Мы встречаемся с ним каждый день.
variations.note: naming the other person with с + instrumental

options.note: using видеться, with none of the dating implication
using вместе to state a relationship — the shortest version

paraphrases.simplest: Мы видимся каждый день. — видеться is safer if you want no ambiguity.

takeaway.note: Они встречаются can mean either, depending on context; видеться carries no romantic sense.

keyPoint: Перестать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "stopping" (pairs with переставать).

grammarFocus.construction: перестань (perfective imperative of перестать) + imperfective infinitive (делать) + the adverb так
grammarFocus.note: перестать means 'to stop' and always takes an imperfective infinitive — перестань делать, never перестань сделать.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses перестаньте

options.note: with Хватит + imperfective infinitive — more forceful
a negative imperative with больше ('don't do that again')

paraphrases.simplest: Перестань. — one word for 'stop it.'

takeaway.note: перестать, прекратить and бросить all take imperfective infinitives — never perfective.

skeleton.note: future 2nd person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Заставить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "forcing" (pairs with заставлять).

grammarFocus.construction: заставишь (perfective future, 2nd person singular of заставить) + accusative (меня) with не
grammarFocus.note: заставить takes an accusative plus an infinitive — 'to make someone do something.' Here the infinitive is left out: 'you won't make me.'

variations.note: formal or plural address uses заставите

variations.ru: Ты не заставишь меня это сделать.
variations.note: adding the infinitive to say what you won't be made to do

options.note: the imperfective future states the intention plainly
using никто for a stronger refusal

paraphrases.simplest: Я не буду. — two words of refusal.

takeaway.pattern: заставить + accusative + infinitive ('to make someone do something')
takeaway.note: Он заставил меня работать. вынудить takes circumstances as subject; заставить takes a person.

keyPoint: Прекратить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "stopping" (pairs with прекращать).

grammarFocus.construction: the impersonal predicate пора + perfective infinitive (прекратить) + accusative (это)
grammarFocus.note: пора usually takes an imperfective infinitive, but a perfective works when the point is bringing something to a definite end. прекратить is 'to put a stop to.'

variations.note: adding the dative нам to name who it concerns
with the imperfective прекращать (a gradual winding down)

options.note: надо + infinitive, more direct
Хватит plus уже — the shortest version

paraphrases.simplest: Хватит уже. — two words for 'enough of this.'

takeaway.pattern: прекратить + accusative or imperfective infinitive ('to stop')
takeaway.note: прекратить разговор (accusative) and прекратить разговаривать (imperfective infinitive) are both correct.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Называть is imperfective, meaning "to call/name" (pairs with назвать).

grammarFocus.construction: the interrogative как + accusative (это) + называешь (imperfective present, 2nd person singular)
grammarFocus.note: называть takes accusative + instrumental ('to call X a Y'). With как + accusative it becomes the set way to ask what something is called.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses называете
the reflexive называется — 'what is this called?', the more natural version

options.note: adding по-русски — the most useful form for a learner
asking what the thing itself is

paraphrases.simplest: Как это называется? — the natural, high-frequency way to ask a word.

takeaway.pattern: Как это называется? ('what is this called?')
takeaway.note: The single most useful question for a learner. Note too the transitive называть + accusative + instrumental.

keyPoint: Отличный is an adjective meaning "excellent, great."

grammarFocus.construction: придумала (perfective past, feminine singular) + accusative (отличный план, adjective plus masculine inanimate)
grammarFocus.note: придумать is the perfective 'to come up with.' отличный means 'excellent,' and the masculine accusative matches the nominative.

variations.note: with a masculine subject the past is придумал
with a feminine noun the accusative is отличную идею

options.note: using найти решение ('to find a solution')
recast as a у + genitive possessive

paraphrases.simplest: Она придумала отличный план. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: придумать план, придумать отговорку ('think up an excuse'). The imperfective придумывать is the thinking-up process.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Ненавидеть is a stative verb with no perfective counterpart; the related возненавидеть ("to come to hate") marks the transition into that state.

replies.gloss: How much longer do we wait?

grammarFocus.construction: ненавижу (imperfective present, 1st person singular) + imperfective infinitive (ждать) + the adverb долго
grammarFocus.note: ненавидеть is a stative verb, 'to hate,' taking an infinitive or an accusative. It has no perfective.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is ненавидим
with an accusative object: 'I hate this job'

options.note: using the set phrase терпеть не могу ('I can't stand')
using не любить — much milder

paraphrases.simplest: Я не люблю ждать. — ненавидеть is strong; this is the safer everyday choice.

takeaway.note: Three degrees: любить, не любить, ненавидеть. терпеть не могу is just as forceful.

keyPoint: Прекрасный is an adjective meaning "beautiful, wonderful."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + the adjective прекрасная + a noun predicate (девушка, nominative)
grammarFocus.note: прекрасный ('wonderful, lovely') agrees with the feminine девушка as прекрасная, and the noun predicate stays nominative.

variations.note: with a masculine noun the adjective is прекрасный

options.note: with замечательная — a near-synonym
using the noun чудо ('a marvel') as predicate, warmer

paraphrases.simplest: Она прекрасная девушка. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: All high praise. Прекрасно! also works as an impersonal predicate meaning 'excellent!'

keyPoint: Оказаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "turning out to be" (pairs with оказываться).

replies.ru: Почему ты думаешь, что она права?
replies.gloss: Why do you think she's right?

grammarFocus.construction: может (3rd person singular of мочь) + perfective infinitive (оказаться) + the short-form adjective права as predicate
grammarFocus.note: оказаться means 'to turn out to be,' and its predicate takes either the instrumental or a short-form adjective. права is the feminine singular short form.

variations.note: with a masculine subject the short form is прав

options.note: using the parenthetical возможно — more compact
with может быть — the most colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Может быть, она права. — the natural version in speech.

takeaway.pattern: оказаться + instrumental or short-form adjective ('to turn out to be')
takeaway.note: Он оказался хорошим врачом (instrumental), Она оказалась права (short form) — both patterns are available.

keyPoint: Важно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it is important."

grammarFocus.construction: знают + a что clause + zero copula + the impersonal predicate важно
grammarFocus.note: важно is a subjectless predicate meaning 'it matters.' The clause что это важно means 'that this matters.'

variations.ru: Они знают, что это было важно.
variations.note: with the clause in the past (было важно)

options.note: using the noun важность — more formal
using небезразлично + dative ('they're not indifferent to it')

paraphrases.simplest: Они знают, что это важно. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: Impersonal predicates важно / нужно / можно (no subject)
takeaway.note: Это важно, Важно понять. The past is было важно and the future будет важно.

keyPoint: Захотеть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "suddenly wanting to" (pairs with хотеть).

replies.gloss: Are you tired from the day?

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb вдруг + захотел (perfective past, masculine singular of захотеть) + infinitive (спать)
grammarFocus.note: захотеть is the perfective of хотеть — the onset of wanting. вдруг ('suddenly') pairs naturally with a perfective.

variations.note: with the impersonal хотелось + dative (more natural)

options.ru: Меня вдруг стало клонить в сон.
options.note: using the idiom клонить в сон ('to feel drowsy')
dative + хотелось + внезапно — the most natural phrasing

paraphrases.simplest: Мне захотелось спать. — the dative construction is the idiomatic Russian choice.

takeaway.pattern: захотеть ('to come to want') / хотеться + dative (impersonal)
takeaway.note: Я захотел ('I wanted') vs Мне захотелось ('a wish came over me'). Russian prefers the dative version.

keyPoint: Давно is an adverb meaning "for a long time, since long ago."

replies.gloss: I've known you a long time too.

grammarFocus.construction: the time adverb давно + imperfective present (знаю) — 'I've known for a long time'
grammarFocus.note: давно plus the present tense expresses something that began earlier and continues now — where English uses the present perfect, Russian uses the present.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is знаем
with a different verb: 'I've lived here a long time'

options.note: using the short-form знакомы ('we've known each other for years')
с + genitive names the starting point: 'since childhood'

paraphrases.simplest: Я давно тебя знаю. — already the simplest and most natural.

takeaway.pattern: давно + imperfective present ('have been doing for a long time')
takeaway.note: Я давно здесь работаю. Careful: давно with a past tense means 'did it long ago' — a different meaning.

keyPoint: Жертва is a feminine noun meaning "victim."

grammarFocus.construction: the interrogative кто + the demonstrative эта + a noun predicate (жертва, a feminine noun)
grammarFocus.note: жертва is grammatically feminine but applies to men too (Он — жертва обмана). кто stays as it is regardless of the predicate's gender.

options.note: the accusative кого with an impersonal 3rd plural: 'who was killed?'
using личность ('identity') — police and press wording

paraphrases.simplest: Кто эта жертва? — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: Nouns whose grammatical gender doesn't match the person (жертва, человек, личность)
takeaway.note: жертва is feminine but used of men as well, and adjectives follow the grammatical gender (невинная жертва).

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Находиться is a stative verb of location with no perfective counterpart.

replies.gloss: I'm already on my way to you.

grammarFocus.construction: the interrogative где + находишься (reflexive imperfective present, 2nd person singular) + the adverb сейчас
grammarFocus.note: находиться means 'to be located' and is more formal than the zero-copula Где ты? The location takes в/на + prepositional.

variations.note: formal or plural address uses находитесь
with an inanimate subject: 'where is the museum?'

options.note: reordered — the most colloquial form
a zero-copula version with no verb (the most natural)

paraphrases.simplest: Ты где? — overwhelmingly what people text and say.

takeaway.pattern: находиться (formal 'to be located') / Где ты? (colloquial zero copula)
takeaway.note: Где находится…? suits buildings and facilities; for people, Где ты? or Ты где? is natural.

skeleton.note: future 1st person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Привести is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "bringing someone" (pairs with приводить).

grammarFocus.construction: приведу (perfective future, 1st person singular of привести) + accusative (тебя) + the directional adverb домой
grammarFocus.note: привести is bringing someone on foot; by vehicle it's привезти. домой takes no preposition.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is приведём

options.note: using проводить ('to see you home') — the most natural
using довести до + genitive ('to walk you as far as home')

paraphrases.simplest: Я провожу тебя домой. — the natural way to offer to see someone home.

takeaway.pattern: привести (to bring on foot) / привезти (to bring by vehicle)
takeaway.note: The вести / везти split runs through all the motion verbs: привести друга, привезти мебель.

keyPoint: Также is a connective adverb meaning "also, likewise."

replies.ru: Я не знал, что ты тоже хочешь.
replies.gloss: I didn't know you wanted to go too.

grammarFocus.construction: the adverb также + хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + perfective infinitive (пойти)
grammarFocus.note: также ('also') belongs to the written register; speech prefers тоже (Я тоже хочу пойти). It sits before what it qualifies.

variations.note: with тоже — the natural colloquial version
with a 1st-person plural subject the verb is хотим

options.note: opening with и to mean 'me too' — compact
можно + с + instrumental: 'may I come with you?'

paraphrases.simplest: Я тоже хочу пойти. — тоже is far more natural in speech.

takeaway.note: Я тоже vs Я также. In negatives, тоже не is the usual choice rather than также не.

keyPoint: Джон is a masculine proper noun from the English name John, which declines like other masculine names.

grammarFocus.construction: a nominative form of address (Джон, a foreign name) + accusative (меня) + слышишь (imperfective present, 2nd person singular)
grammarFocus.note: Foreign names are used in the nominative for address. Джон ends in a consonant, so Russian declines it as a masculine noun (Джона, Джону).

options.note: using тут ('are you there?') — shorter
on a call, the impersonal слышно

paraphrases.simplest: Джон, ты меня слышишь? — the natural way to call out.

takeaway.pattern: Foreign names decline too (Джон / Джона / Джону)
takeaway.note: Consonant-final male names follow the masculine pattern, -а female names the feminine; names in -о, -у or -и stay unchanged.

keyPoint: Понравиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "coming to like" (pairs with нравиться).

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + понравился (perfective past, masculine singular of понравиться) + nominative (этот фильм)
grammarFocus.note: понравиться means 'to please,' so the thing liked is the nominative subject and the person liking it is dative — the reverse of the English framing.

variations.note: with a feminine subject the verb is понравилась
with a plural subject, понравились, and the dative нам

options.note: stating the judgement with an adjective predicate
using быть в восторге от + genitive ('I loved it')

paraphrases.simplest: Мне понравился фильм. — the natural way to give a verdict.

takeaway.note: нравиться (ongoing) vs понравиться (a single verdict). Crucially, the verb agrees with the nominative thing, not the person.

keyPoint: Разговаривать is imperfective, meaning "to converse" (pairs with поговорить).

grammarFocus.construction: хочу (1st person singular of хотеть) + imperfective infinitive (разговаривать) with не
grammarFocus.note: разговаривать means 'to converse' and marks the other person with с + instrumental. The negation plus an imperfective infinitive rejects the activity itself.

variations.note: with a 1st-person plural subject, не хотим

variations.ru: Я не хочу с тобой разговаривать.
variations.note: naming the other person with с + instrumental

options.note: using настроен ('not in the mood to talk')
proposing a postponement — gentler

paraphrases.simplest: Не хочу разговаривать. — dropping the subject is shortest.

takeaway.note: говорить takes о + prepositional for the topic; разговаривать takes с + instrumental for the person. беседовать is the formal 'to converse.'

keyPoint: Выпить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "drinking" (pairs with выпивать).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (2sg хочешь) + perfective infinitive (выпить) + partitive genitive (чаю)
grammarFocus.note: Offering a drink takes the partitive genitive. чай has a special old partitive form чаю, and выпить чаю (have a cup of tea) is a fixed expression.

variations.note: With the accusative чай (implying that specific tea)
Formal/plural plus the indeclinable noun кофе

options.note: The shortest set phrase: the partitive genitive alone
The most colloquial offer, using the future of быть

paraphrases.simplest: Чаю? — one word is enough to make the offer.

takeaway.pattern: выпить чаю / кофе (partitive genitive = a cup of)
takeaway.note: The -у partitive (чаю, сахару, супу) survives in a few masculine nouns; выпить чаю is the most common example.

keyPoint: Сначала is an adverb meaning "first of all."

grammarFocus.construction: sequence adverb сначала + imperative (подумай) + потом + imperative (говори)
grammarFocus.note: сначала... потом... is the set pattern for 'first..., then...'. Note also the aspect contrast: perfective подумай (think once) versus imperfective говори (an ongoing manner of speaking).

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener
With a different first verb (first listen)

options.note: Using прежде чем + infinitive (before doing)
Using the negated verbal adverb не подумав (without thinking)

paraphrases.simplest: Сначала подумай. — the point lands even without the second clause.

takeaway.note: The core sequencing pair. сперва (colloquial) and вначале (bookish) are synonyms.

keyPoint: Близкий is an adjective meaning "close, near."

replies.gloss: You're a close friend of mine too.

grammarFocus.construction: zero-copula sentence + possessive мой + adjective близкий + predicate noun (друг, nominative)
grammarFocus.note: близкий means 'close, intimate'. When two modifiers stack, the possessive comes before the qualitative adjective: мой близкий друг.

variations.note: To a female friend: моя близкая подруга

options.note: Using мы с тобой (you and I) to make both people the subject
Using как + nominative (like a brother) for a warmer tone

paraphrases.simplest: Ты мой близкий друг. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: possessive + qualitative adjective + noun (мой близкий друг)
takeaway.note: Modifier order is possessive, then evaluation, then quality: мой новый красный свитер.

keyPoint: Связь is a feminine noun meaning "connection, signal."

grammarFocus.construction: терять (imperfective present 3pl теряют) + accusative (связь) + в + prepositional (метро, indeclinable)
grammarFocus.note: терять связь (lose signal or contact) is a fixed phrase. связь is a feminine -ь noun whose accusative matches the nominative; метро never changes.

variations.note: The perfective потеряли gives the result: the signal was lost

options.note: The most practical paraphrase, using нет + genitive (there's no signal)
Using пропадать (disappear) with связь as the subject

paraphrases.simplest: В метро нет сигнала. — the most natural way to describe the situation.

takeaway.pattern: терять / потерять связь (lose signal or contact)
takeaway.note: связь covers signal, communication and relationship. потерять связь с кем-то (lose touch with someone) is also very common.

keyPoint: Услышать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "hearing" (pairs with слышать).

replies.ru: Ты уверен, что хочешь это знать?
replies.gloss: Are you sure you want to know?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (1sg хочу) + perfective infinitive (услышать) + accusative (правду)
grammarFocus.note: услышать is the perfective 'to hear (once)', paired with слышать for the ongoing state. The accusative of правда is правду.

variations.note: The imperfective слышать makes it an ongoing wish: always to hear the truth

options.note: The strongest version: a direct imperative
Using знать (to know) instead

paraphrases.simplest: Скажи мне правду. — the most direct way to ask someone for it.

takeaway.note: The same state-versus-moment pairing as видеть/увидеть and знать/узнать. услышать новость (hear the news) is typical.

keyPoint: Похожий is an adjective meaning "similar," combined with на + accusative.

grammarFocus.construction: short-form adjective похож (predicate) + на + accusative (отца, animate masculine = genitive form)
grammarFocus.note: похож is a predicate-only short form that agrees in gender and number (похож/похожа/похожи). The thing resembled goes in на + accusative.

options.note: Using вылитый (the spitting image), colloquial and emphatic
Using напоминать + accusative (to remind one of)

paraphrases.simplest: Ты похож на отца. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: похож на маму; Это похоже на правду (that sounds true). Agreement of the short form plus на + accusative is the key.

keyPoint: Прекрасно is the adverbial form of the adjective прекрасный, meaning "wonderfully."
