grammarFocus.construction: adverb прекрасно + готовить (imperfective present 3pl готовят) + adverb вместе
grammarFocus.note: прекрасно is a manner adverb meaning 'splendidly', marking a high level of skill. As an impersonal predicate it gives Прекрасно! (Wonderful!).

variations.note: With a different verb: they sing beautifully together

options.note: отлично (excellently) is a near-exact synonym
Using получаться (to turn out) for a more concrete compliment

paraphrases.simplest: Они прекрасно готовят. — dropping вместе loses nothing essential.

takeaway.note: All three double as adverbs and impersonal predicates in their -о form. The one-word exclamation Прекрасно! is very frequent.

keyPoint: Агент is a masculine noun meaning "agent."

grammarFocus.construction: zero-copula sentence + adjective хороший + predicate noun (агент, nominative)
grammarFocus.note: агент means 'agent, officer' and is masculine. хороший agrees in the masculine singular nominative, so three words make a complete sentence.

variations.note: For a female agent the noun stays masculine while the adjective goes feminine — a colloquial usage

options.note: Using справляться (to manage well) for a more concrete compliment
Using the predicate noun профессионал (a pro)

paraphrases.simplest: Ты хороший агент. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: many profession nouns have only a masculine form (агент, врач, инженер)
takeaway.note: The masculine noun is used for women too, with the adjective or verb showing gender: Она хороший врач / Врач пришла.

keyPoint: Тысяча is the numeral "a thousand"; the noun takes the genitive plural.

grammarFocus.construction: заплатить (perfective past plural) + numeral тысячу (accusative) + genitive plural (рублей)
grammarFocus.note: тысяча behaves like a noun, so its accusative is тысячу, and the noun that follows goes into the genitive plural (рублей).

variations.note: With две the form is тысячи (genitive singular)
With пять the form is тысяч (genitive plural)

options.note: Using стоить + dative + accusative (it cost them)
Using потратить (to spend)

paraphrases.simplest: Они заплатили тысячу рублей. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: тысяча is a noun-like numeral (тысяча / тысячи / тысяч)
takeaway.note: две тысячи (genitive singular), пять тысяч (genitive plural). The key point is that тысяча itself is governed by the preceding numeral.

keyPoint: Обед is a masculine noun meaning "lunch."

grammarFocus.construction: adverb вместе + готовить (imperfective present 3pl) + accusative (обед, inanimate masculine = nominative form)
grammarFocus.note: вместе means 'together'; placed before the verb it stresses the joint action. обед (lunch) is masculine, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

options.ru: Они готовят обед друг с другом.
options.note: Using друг с другом (with each other), somewhat redundant
Using сообща (jointly), slightly formal

paraphrases.simplest: Они вместе готовят обед. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: вместе stands alone; to name the companion use вместе с ним. совместно (jointly) belongs in official writing.

keyPoint: Собственный is an adjective emphasizing "one's own."

replies.gloss: What kind of business is it?

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + reflexive possessive свой + emphatic adjective собственный + nominative (бизнес)
grammarFocus.note: свой собственный doubles up to stress 'my very own'. собственный alone already means 'own', but the pair intensifies the ownership.

variations.note: With a feminine noun the modifiers become своя собственная
Dropping свой barely changes the meaning

options.note: The most natural paraphrase: работать на себя (be self-employed)
Using дело (business), more idiomatically Russian

paraphrases.simplest: Я работаю на себя. — the most natural way to say you are self-employed.

takeaway.pattern: свой собственный (one's very own: emphatic doubling)
takeaway.note: собственный intensifies ownership; собственными глазами (with my own eyes) is another frequent idiom.

keyPoint: Молодой is an adjective meaning "young."

replies.gloss: You still have it all ahead of you.

grammarFocus.construction: zero-copula sentence + adverb ещё + intensifier очень + long-form adjective predicate (молодой)
grammarFocus.note: ещё means 'still', so очень молодой is 'still very young'. The long-form adjective молодой serves directly as the predicate.

variations.note: With the short form молоды, more categorical and bookish

options.note: An encouraging idiom: everything is still ahead of you

options.ru: Тебе ещё рано об этом думать.
options.note: Using рано (too early) with the dative

paraphrases.simplest: Ты ещё молодой. — dropping очень sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: long-form predicate (Ты молодой) vs short-form predicate (Ты молод)
takeaway.note: The long form describes an inherent quality, the short form a temporary or categorical state. Speech prefers the long form, writing the short one.

skeleton.note: future 1st person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Справиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "managing/handling" (pairs with справляться).

replies.ru: Ты уверен, что тебе не нужна помощь?
replies.gloss: Are you sure you don't need help?
Okay, let me know if you need it.

grammarFocus.construction: emphatic pronoun сам + справиться (perfective future 1sg справлюсь) + с + instrumental (этим)
grammarFocus.note: сам means 'by myself' and agrees with the subject (сам/сама/сами). справиться governs с + instrumental.

options.note: Using без + genitive (without help)
Using negated нужна + dative: I don't need help

paraphrases.simplest: Я сам справлюсь. — dropping с этим is shorter and more forceful.

takeaway.pattern: сам / сама / сами (myself: emphatic pronoun agreeing with the subject)
takeaway.note: Я сам сделаю (I'll do it myself), Она сама пришла (she came herself). самый, meaning 'most', is a different word.

keyPoint: Столько is a quantity determiner meaning "so much," combined with the genitive case.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + quantifier столько + genitive (работы) + exclamatory intonation
grammarFocus.note: столько (so much) is a quantifier taking the genitive. The uncountable noun работа appears as the genitive singular работы. It most often forms an exclamation.

variations.note: With a plural noun: genitive plural дел

options.note: Using много (a lot) for a neutral statement
The idiom быть завален + instrumental (buried in work)

paraphrases.simplest: У меня много работы. — много is the safe neutral choice.

takeaway.pattern: столько + genitive (so much / so many, with exclamatory force)
takeaway.note: столько работы (uncountable: genitive singular), столько людей (countable: genitive plural). так много is nearly synonymous.

keyPoint: Сильно is an adverb meaning "strongly, a lot."

grammarFocus.construction: intensifier сильно + измениться (perfective past masculine singular изменился)
grammarFocus.note: сильно means 'greatly, a lot' and measures the degree of change. изменился is a reflexive perfective giving the result: you have changed.

options.note: An impersonal infinitive idiom: you're unrecognisable
Using стать + instrumental: you've become a different person

paraphrases.simplest: Ты сильно изменился. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: сильно измениться (change a lot), сильно устать (get very tired). сильно is more physical and degree-focused than очень.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, instrumental, the target word

keyPoint: Честь is a feminine noun meaning "honor," with soft-stem declension endings.

grammarFocus.construction: считать + accusative (это) + instrumental (большой честью, feminine singular instrumental)
grammarFocus.note: считать means 'to consider X to be Y' and takes an accusative plus an instrumental. честь is a feminine -ь noun whose instrumental is честью.

variations.note: With a different instrumental: they consider it a mistake

options.note: A more natural paraphrase with для + genitive and a nominative predicate
Using the short passive participle польщены (flattered) with the instrumental

paraphrases.simplest: Для них это большая честь. — the для construction is more natural and easier to follow.

takeaway.pattern: считать + accusative + instrumental (consider X to be Y)
takeaway.note: считать его другом (consider him a friend), считать это ошибкой (consider it a mistake). The predicate noun going into the instrumental is the key.

keyPoint: Отпустить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "letting go" (pairs with отпускать).

grammarFocus.construction: отпустить (perfective imperative отпусти) + accusative (мою руку, feminine singular -ую/-у)
grammarFocus.note: отпустить means 'to let go of'. A feminine noun phrase in the accusative pairs the possessive мою with the noun руку.

variations.note: With a person as the object: let go of me

options.note: Using убрать (take away), a sharper demand
Using the negated imperative of держать (hold)

paraphrases.simplest: Отпусти. — one word for 'let go'.

takeaway.pattern: отпустить + accusative (let go of, let leave)
takeaway.note: отпустить руку (let go of a hand), отпустить домой (let someone go home). Learn it as the opposite of держать (hold).

keyPoint: Секс is a masculine noun meaning "sex."

replies.gloss: What exactly did you talk about?

grammarFocus.construction: говорить (imperfective past plural говорили) + про + accusative (секс)
grammarFocus.note: про is a colloquial preposition meaning 'about' and takes the accusative. Speech prefers it to говорить о + prepositional.

variations.note: With о + prepositional, closer to written style

options.note: A more neutral paraphrase with обсуждать + accusative and тема (topic)
The set phrase речь шла о + prepositional (the talk was about), suitably indirect

paraphrases.simplest: Мы говорили про это. — replacing the noun with это is the safest option.

takeaway.note: про takes the accusative, о the prepositional. Речь шла о... is a handy way to refer to a topic indirectly.

keyPoint: Двое is a collective numeral meaning "the two of (people)," used for counting people.

grammarFocus.construction: collective numeral двое + nominative (они двое) + любить (imperfective present 3pl) + accusative (кофе)
grammarFocus.note: двое is a collective numeral for counting people and takes the genitive (двое детей). Next to a pronoun it gives они двое (the two of them), with emphasis.

options.note: A more natural paraphrase with оба (both)

options.ru: И он, и она любят кофе.
options.note: Using и..., и... (both ... and ...)

paraphrases.simplest: Они оба любят кофе. — оба sounds more natural and is easier to follow.

takeaway.pattern: collective numerals двое / трое / четверо (counting people) + genitive
takeaway.note: двое детей (two children), трое друзей (three friends). Used for male or mixed groups, never for objects.

keyPoint: Ах is an interjection of surprise or regret.

grammarFocus.construction: interjection Ах (set off by a comma) + adverb совсем + perfective past (забыл)
grammarFocus.note: Ах expresses surprise or regret. совсем means 'completely' and can intensify an affirmative too, as in совсем забыл (I completely forgot).

variations.note: With Ой (oops), a lighter kind of surprise

options.note: The idiom вылетело из головы (it flew out of my head)
With an apology attached — the most common real-life version

paraphrases.simplest: Совсем забыл! — dropping the interjection and subject is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: совсем (completely) intensifying both affirmatives and negatives
takeaway.note: совсем забыл (completely forgot) versus совсем не знаю (don't know at all).

keyPoint: Понятно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's clear/understood."

grammarFocus.construction: dative (тебе) + всё + impersonal predicate понятно + question intonation
grammarFocus.note: понятно is an impersonal predicate with no subject; the person who understands goes in the dative. всё is the neuter pronoun 'everything'.

variations.note: To a formal or plural listener: the dative вам

options.note: A more direct check with the perfective past понял
Checking from the other side (any questions?), which sounds polite

paraphrases.simplest: Всё понятно? — dropping the dative is the shortest and most natural check.

takeaway.pattern: dative + понятно (it is clear to someone: impersonal)
takeaway.note: Мне понятно (I see), Непонятно (I don't follow). The most frequent comprehension check in lessons and explanations.

skeleton.note: 3rd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Хотеться is an imperfective impersonal verb meaning "to feel like (doing something)" (pairs with захотеться).

replies.gloss: Are you tired from the day?

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + хотеться (impersonal 3sg хочется) + infinitive (спать)
grammarFocus.note: хотеться is an impersonal verb with no subject; the person who wants something goes in the dative. It sounds softer and more natural than хотеть.

variations.note: With the first person plural dative
Past tense: the neuter form хотелось

options.note: Using хотеть: more direct, stronger intent
The idiom засыпать на ходу (falling asleep on my feet)

paraphrases.simplest: Хочу спать. — dropping the subject is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: dative + хочется + infinitive (feel like doing: impersonal)
takeaway.note: Я хочу states intent; Мне хочется describes a desire that simply arises. Russian strongly favours the softer second option.

keyPoint: Довольно is a degree adverb meaning "quite, fairly."

grammarFocus.construction: intensifier довольно + frequency adverb часто + встречаться (imperfective present 3pl)
grammarFocus.note: довольно means 'fairly, quite' and modifies adverbs and adjectives. довольно часто (quite often) is a stock combination.

options.note: Making the frequency concrete with почти каждый день (almost every day)
With регулярно (regularly), a stiffer register

paraphrases.simplest: Они часто встречаются. — dropping довольно is shortest.

takeaway.note: довольно часто / довольно дорого / довольно интересно. Keep it distinct from достаточно, which means 'sufficiently'.

skeleton.note: 2nd person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Бывать is imperfective, meaning "to be/visit occasionally." The related случиться ("to happen once") differs in that it denotes a single occurrence.

replies.gloss: Is this your first time here?

grammarFocus.construction: frequency adverb часто + бывать (imperfective present 2sg бываешь) + place adverb здесь
grammarFocus.note: бывать is the iterative counterpart of быть, meaning 'to be somewhere regularly, to visit'. Use быть for a single occasion and бывать for repeated visits.

variations.note: The past of быть asks about one occasion: have you been here before?

options.note: Using приходить (to come), more concrete
Checking with the negation of впервые (for the first time)

paraphrases.simplest: Часто здесь бываешь? — dropping the subject sounds most natural in speech.

takeaway.pattern: бывать (be somewhere regularly: iterative) / быть (be, one occasion)
takeaway.note: Contrast Я часто бываю в Москве (I often go to Moscow) with Я был в Москве (I have been to Moscow).

keyPoint: Назвать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "naming" (pairs with называть).

replies.gloss: That's a lovely name for a cat.

grammarFocus.construction: решить (perfective past plural решили) + perfective infinitive (назвать) + accusative (кота, animate masculine = genitive form)
grammarFocus.note: назвать means 'to name' and takes an accusative plus an instrumental (назвать кота Барсиком). кот is animate masculine, so its accusative matches the genitive.

variations.note: The complete version, with the name in the instrumental
With the feminine noun кошка (accusative кошку)

options.note: Using дать имя + dative (to give a name to)
Turned into a question asking what the name is

paraphrases.simplest: Они назвали кота Барсиком. — dropping решили is shorter and clearer.

takeaway.note: назвать сына Иваном (name a son Ivan). The instrumental predicate is shared with считать and называть.

keyPoint: Замечательный is an adjective meaning "wonderful, remarkable."

replies.gloss: How many people are in your family?

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (тебя) + adjective замечательная + nominative (семья)
grammarFocus.note: In the у possession construction the thing possessed stands in the nominative, and the adjective agrees with it. замечательный means 'wonderful', and семья is feminine, hence замечательная.

variations.note: To a formal or plural listener: у вас
With a plural noun: замечательные дети

options.note: Recast with a possessive adjective and zero copula
An exclamation with какой, which strengthens the praise

paraphrases.simplest: У тебя замечательная семья. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: у + genitive + adjective + nominative (someone has a ... )
takeaway.note: The thing possessed is nominative, so the adjective agrees with it. У меня новая работа (I have a new job) follows the same pattern.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Безопасность is a feminine noun meaning "safety, security."

grammarFocus.construction: думать (imperfective present 3pl думают) + о + prepositional (безопасности)
grammarFocus.note: думать takes о + prepositional for what one thinks about. безопасность is a feminine -ь noun, so its prepositional is безопасности.

variations.note: With a different topic (the neuter prepositional будущем)

options.note: Using важна + для + genitive (safety matters to them)
Using заботиться о + prepositional (to take care about)

paraphrases.simplest: Они думают о безопасности. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: Feminine -ость nouns end in -ости in the prepositional (о безопасности, о возможности). думать над + instrumental means to ponder a problem.

keyPoint: Четыре is the numeral "four"; with 2-4 the noun takes the singular genitive.

replies.gloss: That's a lot for one day.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + numeral четыре + genitive singular (урока)
grammarFocus.note: After 2, 3 and 4 the noun goes into the genitive singular (четыре урока); from 5 upwards it switches to the genitive plural (пять уроков). This is the heart of Russian numeral government.

variations.note: From five upwards the genitive plural уроков is used
With a feminine noun: genitive singular встречи

options.note: Using занятие (class) and adding сегодня
Using провести урок (to teach a lesson), from the teacher's side

paraphrases.simplest: У меня четыре урока. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: 2, 3, 4 + genitive singular / 5 and up + genitive plural
takeaway.note: два урока, три урока, четыре урока / пять уроков. Compounds follow their last digit (двадцать два урока).

keyPoint: Прежде is an adverb meaning "before," used together with чем.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective imperative (подумай) + прежде, чем + infinitive (сказать)
grammarFocus.note: прежде чем means 'before' and takes an infinitive when the subject stays the same. подумай is the perfective imperative: think it over once.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener
With a different infinitive: before promising anything

options.note: Using the сначала... потом... sequence
Using the verbal adverb не подумав (without thinking)

paraphrases.simplest: Сначала подумай. — the shortest way to the same point.

takeaway.pattern: прежде чем + infinitive (before doing, same subject)
takeaway.note: With a different subject you need a finite clause (прежде чем он придёт). перед тем как is near-synonymous.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, genitive, the target word

keyPoint: Возможность is a feminine noun meaning "possibility, opportunity."

replies.gloss: Maybe it will come up later.

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + нет + genitive (такой возможности)
grammarFocus.note: нет always takes the genitive. The demonstrative такой agrees in the feminine singular genitive, and возможность becomes возможности.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: такого опыта

options.ru: Я не могу себе этого позволить.
options.note: Using позволить себе (can't afford it)
Using невозможно (impossible), more blunt

paraphrases.simplest: У меня нет такой возможности. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: нет + genitive (there isn't any: negated existence)
takeaway.note: Modifiers go into the genitive too (нет такой возможности, нет свободного времени). Learn it against есть + nominative.

keyPoint: Обо is a euphonic variant of о ("about") used before certain words such as всё.

grammarFocus.construction: perfective imperative (расскажи) + dative (мне) + обо + prepositional (всём)
grammarFocus.note: The preposition о becomes об before a vowel and обо before words like всём and мне for ease of pronunciation. обо всём (about everything) is fixed.

variations.note: Before этом the form is об (об этом)
Addressed to a formal or plural listener

options.note: Using подробности (the details)
Using выкладывать (spill it), colloquial and forceful

paraphrases.simplest: Расскажи всё. — dropping обо всём is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: о / об / обо (the three forms of the preposition о)
takeaway.note: о before consonants (о тебе), об before vowels (об этом), обо before всём, мне, всех (обо всём, обо мне).

skeleton.note: feminine noun, plural accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Мера is a feminine noun meaning "measure," frequent in the plural form меры.

replies.gloss: Agreed, we need to act fast.

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal predicate нужно + perfective infinitive (принять) + accusative (меры, accusative plural)
grammarFocus.note: нужно + infinitive states an obligation with no grammatical subject. принять меры (to take measures) is a set phrase using the accusative plural меры.

variations.note: The dative нам names who is obliged
For the past tense add было

options.note: Using надо + infinitive, more colloquial
Using пора + infinitive (time to act)

paraphrases.simplest: Надо что-то делать. — the most natural version in speech.

takeaway.pattern: принять меры (take measures: a fixed verb-noun pairing)
takeaway.note: принять решение (make a decision), принять участие (take part). принять is the idiomatic verb for abstract nouns like these.

keyPoint: Познакомиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting acquainted" (pairs with знакомиться).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (3pl хотят) + perfective infinitive (познакомиться) + comparative adverb поближе
grammarFocus.note: поближе is the comparative ближе with the prefix по-, softening it to 'a bit closer'. познакомиться поближе means 'to get to know each other better'.

variations.ru: Они хотят познакомиться с твоей семьёй.
variations.note: With с + instrumental naming whom they'll meet

options.ru: Они хотят узнать друг друга получше.
options.note: Using узнать получше (get to know better)
Using хочется with пообщаться (to talk a while longer), softer

paraphrases.simplest: Они хотят познакомиться поближе. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: по- + comparative (поближе, получше, подольше: a bit more ...)
takeaway.note: Adding по- to a comparative makes the request modest. It pairs well with imperatives (Говори погромче = speak up a bit).

keyPoint: Интересно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's interesting."

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + intensifier очень + impersonal predicate интересно + это
grammarFocus.note: интересно is an impersonal predicate with no subject; the interested person goes in the dative. Here это names what the interest is in.

variations.note: With the first person plural dative
For the past tense add было

options.note: A neutral version that drops the dative and makes это the subject
Using интересовать + accusative (it interests me)

paraphrases.simplest: Мне очень интересно. — dropping это sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: dative + интересно (it's interesting to someone: impersonal)
takeaway.note: Мне интересно (I'm interested), Мне было интересно (I found it interesting). Impersonal feeling predicates take the dative plus an -о form.

keyPoint: Затем is a time adverb meaning "then, after that."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective imperative (позвони) + dative (мне) + sequence adverb затем + imperfective imperative (приходи)
grammarFocus.note: затем means 'after that'. The call is a single act, so the perfective позвони fits; the visit is an invitation, so the imperfective приходи is natural.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener

options.note: Spelling out the order with сначала... а потом...
Reordered to stress the call first

paraphrases.simplest: Позвони и приходи. — joining them with и is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: затем / потом (after that: затем is the more bookish of the two)
takeaway.note: затем suits documents, потом conversation. затем also works for listing steps in order.

keyPoint: Рано is an adverb meaning "early."

grammarFocus.construction: perfective past (пришёл, masculine singular) + intensifier слишком + adverb рано
grammarFocus.note: слишком means 'too' and stands before an adjective or adverb. пришёл is the masculine past of прийти, showing its irregular stem change.

options.note: Using рановато (a bit early), softer and colloquial
Dropping the verb and judging the time itself

paraphrases.simplest: Ты слишком рано. — the verb can be left out entirely.

takeaway.note: слишком рано / слишком дорого / слишком много. очень is neutral, слишком carries disapproval.

keyPoint: Чтоб is the colloquial shortened form of чтобы, meaning "in order to."

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective present (звоню) + purpose conjunction чтоб + perfective infinitive (узнать)
grammarFocus.note: чтоб is the colloquial short form of чтобы. With the same subject it takes an infinitive and means 'in order to'.

variations.note: The standard form чтобы, preferred in writing
With a different subject it takes a past-form clause (чтоб ты знал)

options.note: Dropping чтоб and attaching the infinitive directly — the most colloquial option
Using уточнить (to check), politer

paraphrases.simplest: Я звоню узнать. — speech most often drops чтоб.

takeaway.pattern: чтобы / чтоб + infinitive (same subject) / + past form (different subject)
takeaway.note: Я пришёл, чтобы помочь (I came to help) versus Я пришёл, чтобы ты не был один (so that you wouldn't be alone).

keyPoint: Заплатить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "paying" (pairs with платить).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (1sg хочу) + perfective infinitive (заплатить) + instrumental (картой)
grammarFocus.note: The means of payment goes in the instrumental (картой = by card). заплатить is perfective: settling the payment in one completed act.

options.note: можно plus the instrumental — what people actually say at the till
Using принимать (to accept), asking the shop

paraphrases.simplest: Можно картой? — the short form is the natural one in a shop.

takeaway.pattern: instrumental of means (платить картой / наличными / переводом)
takeaway.note: Means and instruments take a bare instrumental: ехать автобусом (go by bus), писать ручкой (write with a pen).

keyPoint: Держаться is imperfective, meaning "to hold on, hang in there." Its perfective varies by meaning; the related продержаться means "to hold out."

grammarFocus.construction: reflexive imperative (держись) + future of быть (будет) + adverb хорошо
grammarFocus.note: держись is the set encouragement 'hold on, hang in there'. The second half uses the future будет in an impersonal 'it will be fine'.

options.note: Using the negated imperative of сдаваться (to give up)
Using обойтись (to turn out all right) — a very Russian way to console

paraphrases.simplest: Держись! — one word carries the encouragement.

takeaway.pattern: Всё будет хорошо (everything will be fine: the future of быть)
takeaway.note: Present tense drops the verb (Всё хорошо), future uses будет, past было. Tense lives entirely in the form of быть.

keyPoint: Странно is an adverb meaning "strangely."

grammarFocus.construction: adverb странно + reflexive pronoun себя (accusative) + вести (imperfective present 3pl ведут)
grammarFocus.note: вести себя means 'to behave'. The reflexive pronoun себя always points back to the subject and has no nominative form.

options.note: Using что-то не так (something's off), more indirect
Making the noun поведение (behaviour) the subject

paraphrases.simplest: Они странно себя ведут. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: вести себя + adverb (to behave in a certain way)
takeaway.note: себя has no nominative and always refers back to the subject. чувствовать себя (to feel) works the same way.

keyPoint: Ой is an interjection of surprise or mild regret.

grammarFocus.construction: interjection Ой (set off by a comma) + perfective imperative (извини) + accusative (меня)
grammarFocus.note: Ой marks surprise or a small slip. извини меня takes an accusative object, though извини alone is just as common.

variations.note: To a formal or plural listener: извините
Using простить (to forgive), warmer and more intimate

options.note: Using прошу прощения (I beg your pardon), politer
Using the short-form adjective виноват (my fault)

paraphrases.simplest: Ой, извини! — dropping меня sounds most natural.

takeaway.note: Извини(те) is slightly more formal, Прости(те) more heartfelt. Ой is the standard little interjection of surprise.

keyPoint: Успокоиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "calming down" (pairs with успокаиваться).

grammarFocus.construction: reflexive perfective imperative (успокойся) + zero-copula clause (всё хорошо)
grammarFocus.note: успокоиться means 'to calm down' and its imperative is успокойся. The second half needs no verb to say 'everything's fine'.

variations.note: With ничего страшного (nothing to worry about)

options.note: Using the negated imperative of волноваться (to worry)
Using дышать глубже (breathe deeper), a concrete way to calm someone

paraphrases.simplest: Успокойся. — one word says it all.

takeaway.pattern: успокоиться (calm down: reflexive) / успокоить (calm someone: transitive)
takeaway.note: Успокойся (you calm down) versus Успокой его (calm him down). The -ся decides whether it's yourself or someone else.

keyPoint: Однажды is an adverb meaning "someday, once."

replies.gloss: What kind of doctor interests you?

grammarFocus.construction: adverb однажды + стать (perfective future 1sg стану) + instrumental (врачом)
grammarFocus.note: стать means 'to become' and puts the predicate noun into the instrumental. однажды means 'one day' and works for both future and past.

options.note: Using когда-нибудь with the future of быть
Adding мечтать (to dream) to state the wish openly

paraphrases.simplest: Я стану врачом. — dropping однажды is shorter and stronger.

takeaway.note: стать врачом / стать другом / стать лучше (лучше is an adverb, so no instrumental). быть takes an instrumental predicate the same way.

keyPoint: Ужасный is an adjective meaning "terrible, awful."

grammarFocus.construction: пережить (perfective past plural пережили) + accusative (ужасный день, inanimate masculine = nominative form)
grammarFocus.note: пережить means 'to live through, to survive'. ужасный is the evaluative adjective 'terrible'.

variations.note: With a feminine noun: ужасную ночь

options.note: Using у + genitive with был (they had a terrible day), more everyday
Using оказаться + instrumental (it turned out terrible)

paraphrases.simplest: У них был ужасный день. — the most natural version in speech.

takeaway.note: пережить войну (survive a war), пережить потерю (get through a loss). For simply 'experience' use испытать.

keyPoint: Миллион is a masculine noun meaning "million."

replies.ru: Что бы ты сделал с этими деньгами?
replies.gloss: What would you do with that money?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (1sg хочу) + the accusative numeral миллион + genitive plural (рублей)
grammarFocus.note: миллион behaves like a noun, and the noun after it always stands in the genitive plural (миллион рублей). Its accusative matches the nominative.

variations.note: With два the form is миллиона (genitive singular)
With a different currency: genitive plural долларов

options.note: Using нужен + nominative (I need a million)
Using мечтать о + prepositional (to dream of)

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу миллион. — рублей can be left to context.

takeaway.pattern: миллион / миллиард + genitive plural (noun-like numerals, as with тысяча)
takeaway.note: миллион рублей, два миллиона рублей, пять миллионов рублей. The numeral itself declines.

keyPoint: Другие is the plural of другой, meaning "other."

replies.gloss: Did they come to a conclusion?

grammarFocus.construction: обсуждать (imperfective present 3pl обсуждают) + accusative (другие варианты, accusative plural)
grammarFocus.note: другой means 'other, different'. In the inanimate plural its accusative matches the nominative (другие варианты). обсуждать takes a direct accusative.

variations.note: With a different subject and noun: обсуждаем

options.note: Using рассматривать (to consider) with альтернативы, more formal
Using думать о + prepositional (plural вариантах)

paraphrases.simplest: Они обсуждают другие варианты. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: the declension of другой: другой / другая / другие / других
takeaway.note: In the inanimate plural the accusative equals the nominative (другие варианты); for animates it equals the genitive (других людей).

keyPoint: Иначе is a connective adverb meaning "otherwise."

replies.gloss: Okay, I'll do it that way.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective imperative (делай) + adverb так + conjunction иначе + future of быть (будет плохо)
grammarFocus.note: иначе means 'otherwise' and introduces the warning. будет плохо is impersonal: things will turn out badly.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener

variations.ru: Делай так, а то будет плохо.
variations.note: With а то (or else), more colloquial

options.ru: Если не сделаешь так, будет плохо.
options.note: Spelling out the condition with если не
Using лучше (you'd better), a softer piece of advice

paraphrases.simplest: Делай так, а то будет плохо. — а то is the natural choice in speech.

takeaway.pattern: иначе / а то (otherwise: introducing a warning)
takeaway.note: иначе is bookish, а то colloquial. Поторопись, а то опоздаешь (hurry up or you'll be late) is the classic example.

keyPoint: Заняться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting down to" something (pairs with заниматься).

replies.gloss: Okay, I won't get in the way.

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + impersonal predicate надо + perfective infinitive (заняться) + instrumental (делом)
grammarFocus.note: заняться takes the instrumental and means 'to take up, get down to'. надо + infinitive has no subject, and the dative names who must act.

variations.note: With the first person plural dative
With a different instrumental: take up sport

options.note: Using приниматься за + accusative (to get down to it)
Using хватит + infinitive (enough loafing about), much blunter

paraphrases.simplest: Надо заняться делом. — dropping the dative is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: заняться + instrumental (take up, get down to)
takeaway.note: заняться делом / спортом / музыкой. The imperfective заниматься means to be engaged in something or to study.

keyPoint: Согласен is the short form of согласный, used in predicate position to mean "in agreement."

replies.ru: Не совсем, у меня другое мнение.
replies.gloss: Not quite, I have a different opinion.

grammarFocus.construction: short-form adjective predicate (согласен) + с + instrumental (мной) + question intonation
grammarFocus.note: согласен is a predicate-only short form agreeing in gender and number (согласен/согласна/согласны). The person you agree with goes in с + instrumental.

options.ru: Ты со мной согласен или нет?
options.note: Adding или нет to press for an answer
A more open question asking for the opinion itself

paraphrases.simplest: Согласен? — one word is enough.

takeaway.note: The preposition с becomes со before м- (со мной, со всеми). Learn it together with the agreement of the short form.

keyPoint: Приятно is an impersonal predicate meaning "it's pleasant/nice."

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + impersonal predicate приятно + imperfective infinitive (слышать) + accusative (это)
grammarFocus.note: приятно is an impersonal predicate with no subject; the person who feels it goes in the dative. Мне приятно это слышать is the set reply to a compliment.

variations.note: With the first person plural dative
For the past tense add было

options.note: With thanks attached — the most common real-life reply
Using the short-form adjective рад (glad)

paraphrases.simplest: Очень приятно. — two words say it all.

takeaway.pattern: dative + приятно + infinitive (it's pleasant for someone to ...)
takeaway.note: Мне приятно (that's nice to hear), Очень приятно (pleased to meet you). It is also the standard greeting on first meeting.

skeleton.note: 3rd person plural present, the target word

keyPoint: Звучать is imperfective, meaning "to sound" (pairs with прозвучать).

grammarFocus.construction: звучать (imperfective present 3pl звучат) + intensifier очень + manner adverb дружелюбно
grammarFocus.note: звучать means 'to sound' of a voice or wording, and the manner is given by an adverb — the -о form, never an adjective.

variations.note: With это as subject: that sounds strange

options.note: Using говорить with the adverb (they speak warmly)
Using the noun тон (tone) with an adjective

paraphrases.simplest: Они звучат дружелюбно. — dropping очень is shortest.

takeaway.note: Это звучит хорошо (that sounds good), Звучит заманчиво (sounds tempting). Like English 'sound', but always with an adverb.

keyPoint: Обратно is an adverb meaning "back."

replies.gloss: Are you tired from the trip?

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (1sg хочу) + directional adverb обратно + directional adverb домой
grammarFocus.note: обратно means 'back' and домой 'homewards'. Both are adverbs, so they take no preposition and never decline.

variations.note: With в + accusative naming the destination

options.note: Adding the verb вернуться (to return) for a fuller sentence
An imperative invitation — the most practical version

paraphrases.simplest: Хочу домой. — dropping the subject and обратно sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: домой / обратно / туда (directional adverbs that take no preposition)
takeaway.note: Don't mix дома (at home: location) with домой (homewards: direction). обратно домой conveys heading back home.

keyPoint: Приятель is a casual masculine noun meaning "buddy, pal."

replies.gloss: Have you known each other long?

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + possessive мой + adjective старый + predicate noun (приятель)
grammarFocus.note: приятель is a masculine noun for a friend or mate — less close than друг. старый приятель means a friend of long standing.

options.note: Using знакомы (we've known each other a long time)
Using друг с детства (a childhood friend) to make the bond specific

paraphrases.simplest: Он мой старый приятель. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: друг / приятель / знакомый (three degrees of closeness)
takeaway.note: друг is closest, приятель a congenial acquaintance, знакомый merely someone you know. Russian keeps these distinct.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Доверять is an imperfective stative verb; the related довериться ("to trust and place oneself in someone's hands") differs in meaning.

grammarFocus.construction: dative (тебе) + adverb полностью + доверять (imperfective present 1sg доверяю)
grammarFocus.note: доверять means 'to trust' and takes the dative, not the accusative — a classic stumbling block for learners.

variations.note: To a formal or plural listener: the dative вам

options.note: Using верить + dative (to believe), more everyday

options.ru: У меня нет к тебе никаких сомнений.
options.note: Using сомнения (doubts), formal and emphatic

paraphrases.simplest: Я тебе доверяю. — dropping полностью sounds most natural.

takeaway.note: One of the dative-governing verbs, alongside верить (believe), помогать (help) and звонить (call).

keyPoint: Насколько is an interrogative adverb meaning "how much."

grammarFocus.construction: interrogative adverb насколько + short-form adjective predicate (уверен)
grammarFocus.note: насколько asks 'to what extent'. уверен is a predicate-only short form agreeing in gender and number (уверен/уверена/уверены).

options.note: Using точно (really), a shorter check
Using the negation of сомневаться в + prepositional (to doubt)

paraphrases.simplest: Ты уверен? — dropping насколько is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: уверен в + prepositional (to be sure of)
takeaway.note: Я уверен в себе (I'm confident), Я уверен в этом (I'm sure of it). насколько is a handy way to ask about degree.

keyPoint: Двигаться is imperfective, meaning "to move" (pairs with двинуться).

replies.gloss: Why do I have to stand here?

grammarFocus.construction: negated imperfective imperative (не двигайся) + imperfective imperative (стой)
grammarFocus.note: Prohibitions use the imperfective imperative (не двигайся = don't move). стой, from стоять, means 'stay put'.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener

options.note: Using на месте (stay where you are), the shortest command
Using ни шагу (not a step), a sharp prohibition

paraphrases.simplest: Стой! — one word is enough.

takeaway.pattern: prohibitions take the imperfective imperative (не делай, не двигайся)
takeaway.note: A negated perfective imperative (не сделай) warns against doing something accidentally. Prohibition and warning pick different aspects.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Ситуация is a feminine noun meaning "situation."

grammarFocus.construction: обсуждать (imperfective present 3pl) + accusative (ситуацию) + после + genitive (свидания)
grammarFocus.note: после means 'after' and takes the genitive. The accusative of ситуация is ситуацию.

variations.note: With a different genitive: after work

options.ru: После свидания они говорят о том, что было.
options.note: Using говорить о + prepositional with a reordered clause
Using разбирать (to go over in detail)

paraphrases.simplest: Они обсуждают ситуацию после свидания. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: после обеда (after lunch), перед обедом (before lunch). The case changes with the direction in time.

skeleton.note: masculine noun, plural genitive, the target word

keyPoint: Доллар is a masculine noun meaning "dollar."

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + adverb только + numeral сто + genitive plural (долларов)
grammarFocus.note: сто (a hundred) takes the genitive plural (сто долларов). только means 'only' and stresses how little it is.

variations.note: With a different currency: genitive plural рублей
With всего (just), almost the same meaning

options.ru: У меня при себе сто долларов.
options.note: Using при себе (on me)

options.ru: Больше ста долларов у меня нет.
options.note: Turned into a negation with нет + genitive (I don't have more than a hundred)

paraphrases.simplest: У меня сто долларов. — dropping только is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: 5 and up, сто, тысяча + genitive plural (сто долларов)
takeaway.note: 2-4 take the genitive singular (два доллара); 5 and above the genitive plural (пять долларов, сто долларов).

keyPoint: Клиент is a masculine noun meaning "client."

grammarFocus.construction: possessive наш + nominative (клиент) + adverb уже + ждать (imperfective present 3sg ждёт)
grammarFocus.note: наш means 'our' and its masculine singular nominative is наш. ждать has a shifting stem (жду, ждёшь, ждёт).

options.note: Using на месте (the client is already here)
An impersonal third person plural (we're already being waited for)

paraphrases.simplest: Клиент уже ждёт. — наш can be left out.

takeaway.pattern: agreement of наш / наша / наше / наши
takeaway.note: наш клиент, наша работа, наше дело, наши планы. It declines like мой and always agrees with its noun.

keyPoint: Достать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "getting hold of" something (pairs with доставать).

grammarFocus.construction: interrogative где + достать (perfective past masculine singular достал) + accusative (билеты, accusative plural)
grammarFocus.note: достать is the colloquial perfective 'to get hold of'. The inanimate plural accusative matches the nominative (билеты).

options.note: Using купить (to buy), neutral
Using откуда with у + genitive (where did you get the tickets?), colloquial

paraphrases.simplest: Где ты взял билеты? — взять is the plainest option.

takeaway.pattern: достать (to get hold of, with effort: colloquial)
takeaway.note: достать билеты (score tickets). купить is simply 'buy'; достать implies the thing was hard to come by.

keyPoint: Кстати is a parenthetical adverb meaning "by the way."

grammarFocus.construction: nominative (они) + parenthetical кстати (between commas) + adverb уже + perfective past (приехали)
grammarFocus.note: кстати means 'by the way' and is set off by commas. It can stand at the start of the sentence or inside it.

variations.note: With the parenthetical at the front

options.note: Using между прочим (incidentally)
Using Да, и... (yes, and) to add the information

paraphrases.simplest: Кстати, они приехали. — dropping уже is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: parentheticals are set off by commas (кстати, конечно, например, во-первых)
takeaway.note: кстати means 'by the way'. Parentheticals aren't sentence parts, so they govern no case and always take commas.

keyPoint: Разобраться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "figuring something out" (pairs with разбираться).

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + impersonal надо + perfective infinitive (разобраться) + во + prepositional (всём)
grammarFocus.note: разобраться means 'to get to the bottom of' and takes в + prepositional. Before всём the preposition в becomes во for ease of pronunciation.

variations.note: With этом the plain в is used (в этом)
With the first person plural dative

options.note: Using понять (to understand), simpler
Using выяснить обстоятельства (establish the circumstances), formal

paraphrases.simplest: Надо разобраться. — dropping во всём is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: the preposition в becomes во before some clusters (во всём, во Франции, во вторник)
takeaway.note: Learn it together with the government разобраться в чём-то (to get to grips with something).

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Проводить here is an imperfective verb meaning "to walk/see someone home" — a different sense from the identically spelled but differently stressed проводить ("to spend time").

replies.gloss: No need, I can get there myself.

grammarFocus.construction: проводить (perfective future 1sg провожу) + accusative (тебя) + до + genitive (дома)
grammarFocus.note: проводить means 'to walk someone somewhere', with the destination in до + genitive. Here провожу is the perfective future, which makes it an offer.

variations.note: To a formal or plural listener: the accusative вас
With a different destination: до метро

options.note: Adding давай to soften the offer

options.ru: Я пойду с тобой до дома.
options.note: Using пойти с + instrumental (I'll go with you)

paraphrases.simplest: Я тебя провожу. — dropping до дома sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: до + genitive (as far as, up to)
takeaway.note: до дома (as far as home), до конца (to the end), до завтра (see you tomorrow). Also half of от... до... (from ... to ...).

skeleton.note: neuter noun, prepositional, the target word

keyPoint: Будущее is a substantivized adjective (from будущий) functioning as a neuter noun meaning "the future."

replies.gloss: What exactly are you thinking about?

grammarFocus.construction: думать (imperfective present 1sg думаю) + о + prepositional (будущем)
grammarFocus.note: будущее is a neuter noun formed from an adjective, so it declines like one (будущее / будущего / о будущем).

variations.note: прошлое (the past) declines the same adjectival way
Adding a genitive: the children's future

options.note: Using беспокоить + accusative (the future worries me)
Using планы на будущее (plans for the future), more concrete

paraphrases.simplest: Я думаю о будущем. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: They keep adjective endings but work as nouns: в будущем (in the future), о прошлом (about the past).

keyPoint: Некоторые is the plural of некоторый, meaning "some."

grammarFocus.construction: indefinite pronoun некоторые + nominative plural (люди) + adverb так + думать (3pl думают)
grammarFocus.note: некоторые means 'some' and declines like an adjective, always in the plural. It can also stand alone: Некоторые думают...

variations.note: With некоторые alone as the subject
With из + genitive (some of them) to limit the group

options.note: Using a который clause, more explicit
Using кто-то with считать (some really do think so)

paraphrases.simplest: Некоторые так думают. — dropping люди sounds most natural.

takeaway.pattern: некоторые (some: an indefinite pronoun with adjectival endings)
takeaway.note: некоторые люди, в некоторых случаях, некоторым нравится. On its own it means 'some people'.

keyPoint: Простой is an adjective meaning "simple."

grammarFocus.construction: выбрать (perfective past plural выбрали) + accusative (простой десерт, inanimate masculine = nominative form)
grammarFocus.note: выбрать means 'to choose' and its past stem shifts (выбрать → выбрали). простой means 'simple, plain'.

variations.note: With a neuter noun: простое платье

options.note: Using остановиться на + prepositional (to settle on)
Using the noun выбор (choice) in a zero-copula sentence

paraphrases.simplest: Они выбрали простой десерт. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: простой десерт (a plain dessert), простой вопрос (an easy question). The adverb просто (simply, just) is extremely frequent.

keyPoint: Преступление is a neuter noun meaning "crime."

grammarFocus.construction: обсуждать (imperfective present 3pl) + accusative (преступление) + в + prepositional (сериале)
grammarFocus.note: преступление is a -ние neuter noun, so its accusative matches the nominative. в сериале gives the setting in the prepositional.

variations.note: With a different prepositional: в книге
Changing the object and the subject to the first person plural

options.ru: Они говорят о преступлении из сериала.
options.note: Using из + genitive to mark where the crime comes from
Using сюжет (the plot), more concrete

paraphrases.simplest: Они обсуждают преступление в сериале. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: All neuter, accusative equals nominative, prepositional in -нии (в преступлении). The commonest way Russian builds abstract nouns.

skeleton.note: 1st person singular present, the target word

keyPoint: Уметь is a stative verb of ability; the related научиться ("to learn/become able") differs in meaning.

grammarFocus.construction: уметь (imperfective present 1sg умею) + imperfective infinitive (готовить)
grammarFocus.note: уметь means 'to know how to' — an acquired skill — and takes an infinitive. The contrast with мочь (to be able, circumstantially) is the point.

options.note: Using мочь for circumstantial ability (I can make something)
Dropping уметь and showing the skill with готовить plus an adverb

paraphrases.simplest: Я умею готовить. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: уметь (know how to) / мочь (be able to in the circumstances)
takeaway.note: Я умею плавать (I can swim — a skill) versus Я могу плавать (I'm allowed or able to swim now). English 'can' splits in two.

keyPoint: Сей is an archaic demonstrative pronoun meaning "this," surviving in modern Russian mainly in fixed expressions like "на сей раз."

grammarFocus.construction: на + accusative (сей раз) + nominative (я) + short-form adjective predicate (согласен)
grammarFocus.note: сей is the archaic demonstrative 'this', surviving in fixed phrases like на сей раз (this time). Modern Russian uses этот.

variations.note: With the modern этот — the ordinary version

options.note: Using сейчас (right now), more everyday

options.ru: В этом случае я не против.
options.note: Using не против (I don't object), more measured

paraphrases.simplest: На этот раз я согласен. — этот is the natural modern choice.

takeaway.pattern: сей (this: archaic) survives in fixed phrases
takeaway.note: на сей раз (this time), до сих пор (until now), сию минуту (this instant). In everyday speech always этот.

keyPoint: Следить is imperfective, meaning "to watch over/mind" (pairs with проследить).

replies.gloss: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend.

grammarFocus.construction: следить (imperfective imperative следи) + за + instrumental (своими словами, instrumental plural)
grammarFocus.note: следить takes за + instrumental and means 'to watch, keep an eye on'. The reflexive possessive свой points back to the subject, giving the plural instrumental своими.

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener
With a different instrumental: keep an eye on the child

options.note: Using выбирать слова (choose your words)
Using что говоришь (think what you're saying), blunter

paraphrases.simplest: Следи за словами. — dropping своими is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: следить за + instrumental (watch, keep an eye on)
takeaway.note: следить за здоровьем (look after your health), следить за новостями (follow the news). The за + instrumental is fixed.

skeleton.note: future 3rd person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Закончиться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "ending" (pairs with заканчиваться).

replies.gloss: How long has it been going on?

grammarFocus.construction: надеяться (imperfective present 3pl надеются) + что clause + perfective future (закончится)
grammarFocus.note: надеяться takes a что clause. закончиться is a reflexive perfective meaning 'to come to an end', with the event as its subject.

variations.ru: Я надеюсь, что встреча скоро закончится.
Они надеются, что всё закончится хорошо.
variations.note: Adding an adverb: that it will all end well

options.note: Using the noun конец (end), shorter
Using хоть бы with a past form to express the wish

paraphrases.simplest: Надеюсь, встреча скоро закончится. — что can be dropped.

takeaway.pattern: закончиться (something ends: reflexive) / закончить (to end something: transitive)
takeaway.note: Встреча закончилась (the meeting ended) versus Он закончил встречу (he ended the meeting). The -ся decides which.

keyPoint: Устроить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "organizing/throwing" something (pairs with устраивать).

grammarFocus.construction: устроить (perfective past plural устроили) + accusative (маленький праздник)
grammarFocus.note: устроить means 'to arrange, put on'. маленький means 'small', and its masculine singular accusative matches the nominative.

variations.note: With a different adjective: a big celebration
With a feminine noun: маленькую вечеринку

options.note: Using организовать (to organise), slightly formal
Using у + genitive with был (they had a small celebration)

paraphrases.simplest: Они устроили праздник. — dropping маленький is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: устроить + accusative (put on an event, arrange)
takeaway.note: устроить праздник (throw a party), устроить скандал (make a scene), устроиться на работу (get a job).

keyPoint: Добро is a neuter noun meaning "good, kindness."

grammarFocus.construction: помнить (imperfective present 3pl помнят) + accusative (твоё добро)
grammarFocus.note: добро is a neuter noun meaning 'good, kindness', and its accusative matches the nominative. The possessive твоё agrees in the neuter singular.

variations.note: With доброта (kindness): the feminine accusative твою доброту

options.ru: Они не забыли, что ты сделал.
options.note: Using не забыли (haven't forgotten) with a что clause
Using благодарны + dative (they're grateful to you)

paraphrases.simplest: Они помнят твоё добро. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: помнить + accusative (to remember: an imperfective-only state verb)
takeaway.note: помнить has no true perfective; запомнить (commit to memory) and вспомнить (recall) cover the other meanings.

keyPoint: Любимый is an adjective meaning "favorite, beloved."

grammarFocus.construction: включить (perfective past plural включили) + accusative (любимую песню, feminine singular accusative)
grammarFocus.note: включить means 'to switch on, put on'. любимая means 'favourite', and its feminine singular accusative is любимую.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: любимый фильм

options.note: Using поставить (to put on), specific to music
Using зазвучать (to start playing) with the song as subject

paraphrases.simplest: Они включили любимую песню. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: включить свет (turn on the light), выключить телефон (turn off the phone). The most-used everyday pair.

keyPoint: Полицейский is a substantivized adjective functioning as a masculine noun meaning "police officer."

grammarFocus.construction: demonstrative этот + adjectival noun (полицейский) + intensifier очень + adjective predicate (добрый)
grammarFocus.note: полицейский is a noun with adjective endings, so it declines like one (полицейского, полицейскому), and этот agrees with it.

options.ru: Этот полицейский хорошо к нам отнёсся.
options.note: Using отнестись к + dative (he treated us well), more concrete
Using оказаться + instrumental (he turned out to be kind)

paraphrases.simplest: Этот полицейский очень добрый. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: Adjectives in form, nouns in function, with adjectival declension. Feminine полицейская, plural полицейские.

keyPoint: Подобный is an adjective meaning "similar, such."

grammarFocus.construction: negated perfective past (не видел) + genitive (подобного) + adverb раньше
grammarFocus.note: A negated verb can put its object into the genitive. подобное (such a thing) becomes the neuter genitive подобного. The genitive of negation is preferred for vague, non-specific objects.

variations.note: A female speaker says не видела
With the set phrase ничего подобного (nothing of the kind)

options.note: Fronting такого (that sort of thing) for emphasis
Using впервые (for the first time), simpler

paraphrases.simplest: Такого я раньше не видел. — такого sounds more natural in speech.

takeaway.note: Я не вижу проблемы (I don't see a problem). Vague objects take the genitive; a specific one may keep the accusative (Я не видел этот фильм).

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Штука is a colloquial feminine noun meaning "thing, item."

grammarFocus.construction: купить (perfective past plural купили) + accusative (полезную штуку, feminine singular accusative)
grammarFocus.note: штука is the handy colloquial feminine noun for 'thing'. Its accusative is штуку, and the adjective agrees as полезную.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: полезный прибор

options.note: Using вещь (thing), more neutral
Using приобрести (to acquire), formal

paraphrases.simplest: Они купили полезную штуку. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: штука (thing: colloquial) / вещь (thing: neutral) / предмет (item: formal)
takeaway.note: штука also counts items (три штуки = three of them), and в чём штука? means 'what's the catch?'.

skeleton.note: future 3rd person singular, the target word

keyPoint: Понадобиться is a perfective impersonal verb meaning "to become necessary," with no corresponding imperfective.

grammarFocus.construction: знать (3pl знают) + colon + dative (им) + понадобиться (perfective future понадобится) + nominative (помощь)
grammarFocus.note: понадобиться means 'to be needed': the person goes in the dative and the thing needed is the subject. The colon introduces the explanation.

variations.ru: Они знают, что им понадобится помощь.
variations.note: The standard version with a что clause
With the first person singular dative

options.note: Using нужна with будет (they will need help)
Using без + genitive (they won't manage without help)

paraphrases.simplest: Им понадобится помощь. — dropping the first clause is shortest.

takeaway.pattern: dative + понадобиться + nominative (someone will need something)
takeaway.note: Мне понадобятся деньги (I'll need money — plural takes понадобятся). As with нужен, the thing needed is the subject.

keyPoint: Совершенно is an intensifying adverb meaning "completely."

grammarFocus.construction: intensifier совершенно + perfective past (забыл, masculine singular)
grammarFocus.note: совершенно means 'completely, utterly'. It is close to совсем but somewhat more formal and at home in writing.

variations.note: Adding об этом with a first person plural subject

options.note: Using совсем, more colloquial
The idiom вылетело из головы (it flew out of my head)

paraphrases.simplest: Совсем забыл. — dropping the subject is the natural spoken form.

takeaway.note: совершенно is formal, совсем colloquial, абсолютно a loanword. совершенно верно (absolutely right) is the set way to agree.

keyPoint: Сходить is perfective, meaning "to go somewhere and come back" (a round trip); its corresponding imperfective is ходить (multidirectional).

grammarFocus.construction: dative (мне) + impersonal надо + perfective infinitive (сходить) + в + accusative (магазин)
grammarFocus.note: сходить is the perfective 'to go and come back' — one round trip. The contrast with пойти (to set off) is the point; direction goes in в + accusative.

variations.note: With the first person plural dative
пойти shifts the focus to setting off for the shop

options.note: Using забежать (pop in), more colloquial
Using за + instrumental (out for groceries) with the verb dropped

paraphrases.simplest: Надо в магазин. — speech often drops the verb too.

takeaway.pattern: сходить (go and come back: one round trip) / пойти (set off)
takeaway.note: Я сходил в аптеку (I've been to the chemist) versus Я пошёл в аптеку (I set off for the chemist). сходить implies you're already back.

skeleton.note: feminine noun, accusative, the target word

keyPoint: Запись is a feminine noun meaning "recording."

grammarFocus.construction: слушать (imperfective present 1sg слушаю) + accusative (новую запись, feminine singular accusative)
grammarFocus.note: запись is a feminine -ь noun, so its accusative matches the nominative. Only the adjective shows the case, as новую.

variations.note: A different noun and subject: слушаем

options.note: Using играть (is playing) with the recording as subject
Using включить (to put on)

paraphrases.simplest: Я слушаю новую запись. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: feminine -ь nouns have accusative = nominative (запись, связь, помощь)
takeaway.note: The adjective shows the case with its -ую ending, so the modifier is where you read the grammar (слушаю новую запись).

keyPoint: Небольшой is an adjective meaning "small, not big."

grammarFocus.construction: у + genitive (меня) + adjective небольшая + nominative (проблема)
grammarFocus.note: небольшой means 'not big, slight', built with the fused negative prefix не-. It sounds more measured and indirect than маленький.

variations.note: With a masculine noun: небольшой вопрос

options.note: Using маленькая, more direct
Recast as a request with помощь (help)

paraphrases.simplest: У меня небольшая проблема. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.note: The prefix makes the word understated and polite. неплохо (not bad = rather good) is a very Russian way to praise.

keyPoint: Мужик is a colloquial masculine noun meaning "guy, man."

grammarFocus.construction: zero copula + adjective хороший + predicate noun (мужик)
grammarFocus.note: мужик is a colloquial masculine noun for a man or bloke. хороший мужик means 'a good guy' and has no place in polite settings.

variations.note: With человек (person), neutral and usable anywhere

options.note: Using нормальный парень (a decent bloke), equally colloquial
Using положиться на + accusative (he can be relied on)

paraphrases.simplest: Он хороший человек. — the version that fits any setting.

takeaway.note: мужик is warm but rough, so use мужчина or человек at work or with strangers.

keyPoint: Взглянуть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "taking a glance" (pairs with взглядывать, though that imperfective is rare).

replies.gloss: What exactly do you want to see?

grammarFocus.construction: дать (perfective imperative дай) + dative (мне) + perfective infinitive (взглянуть)
grammarFocus.note: дать + dative + infinitive is the set way to ask to be allowed to do something. взглянуть is the perfective 'to take a look'.

variations.note: With a different infinitive: let me think

options.note: Using можно + infinitive (may I look?), politer
Using the imperative of показать (show me)

paraphrases.simplest: Можно посмотреть? — the shortest polite way to ask.

takeaway.pattern: дать + dative + infinitive (let someone do something)
takeaway.note: Дай мне сказать (let me speak), Дай ему отдохнуть (let him rest). позволить + dative + infinitive is the formal equivalent.

keyPoint: Пропасть is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "disappearing" (pairs with пропадать).

grammarFocus.construction: interrogative куда + perfective past (пропал, masculine singular)
grammarFocus.note: пропасть means 'to vanish, go missing'. Куда ты пропал? is the standard friendly 'where have you been hiding?'.

options.note: Using не было слышно (why haven't I heard from you?)
Using не видно (haven't seen you in ages), gentler

paraphrases.simplest: Ты куда пропал? — the reordered colloquial version is just as natural.

takeaway.note: Ключи пропали (the keys have gone), Пропал аппетит (my appetite's gone). It works for people and things alike.

keyPoint: Выяснить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "clarifying" something (pairs with выяснять).

grammarFocus.construction: хотеть (1sg хочу) + perfective infinitive (выяснить) + accusative (правду)
grammarFocus.note: выяснить means 'to find out, establish'. The accusative of правда is правду.

variations.note: With a different object: все детали (accusative plural)

options.note: Using знать (to know), simpler
Using добраться до + genitive (I'll get to the truth), forceful

paraphrases.simplest: Я хочу знать правду. — знать is plainer and carries further.

takeaway.pattern: выяснить (establish by investigating) / узнать (find out, be told)
takeaway.note: выяснить обстоятельства is investigation; узнать новость is simply receiving the news.

keyPoint: Угодно is a particle meaning "whatever (you like)," used in indefinite expressions like что угодно.

replies.gloss: Okay, I have a lot of questions.

grammarFocus.construction: imperfective imperative (спрашивай) + что угодно (anything at all)
grammarFocus.note: угодно is an invariable particle that combines with question words to mean 'any' (что угодно, где угодно, когда угодно).

variations.note: Addressed to a formal or plural listener

options.note: Using всё, что хочешь (whatever you like)
Using любые вопросы (any questions at all)

paraphrases.simplest: Спрашивай что хочешь. — что хочешь is the more natural spoken choice.

takeaway.pattern: question word + угодно (что угодно, где угодно, кто угодно)
takeaway.note: This builds 'anything, anywhere, anyone'. угодно never changes; the question word declines (кому угодно).

keyPoint: Поступить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "acting" a certain way (pairs with поступать).

grammarFocus.construction: решить (perfective past plural решили) + interrogative как + perfective infinitive (поступить)
grammarFocus.note: A question word plus an infinitive means 'how to do something'. поступить is the perfective 'to act, behave'.

options.note: Using принять решение (make a decision)
Using определиться с + instrumental (to settle on)

paraphrases.simplest: Они решили, как поступить. — already the simplest form.

takeaway.pattern: question word + infinitive (как поступить, что делать, куда идти)
takeaway.note: A handy subjectless construction. Не знаю, что делать (I don't know what to do) is the classic case.

keyPoint: Вызвать is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "calling/summoning" (pairs with вызывать).

grammarFocus.construction: impersonal надо + perfective infinitive (вызвать) + accusative (врача, animate masculine = genitive form)
grammarFocus.note: вызвать means 'to call out, send for' and is the standard verb for calling a doctor or ambulance. врач is animate, so its accusative matches the genitive.

variations.note: With скорая (an ambulance): the adjectival noun's accusative скорую
With the dative нам and the indeclinable такси

options.note: Using нужен + nominative (a doctor is needed) — the shortest version
Using позвонить в + accusative (call the ambulance service)

paraphrases.simplest: Нужен врач. — two words carry the urgency.

takeaway.note: вызвать врача / скорую / такси / полицию. звать is calling out by voice; вызвать is arranging for someone to come.

keyPoint: Пригласить is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "inviting" (pairs with приглашать).

takeaway.pattern: пригласить + accusative + на / в + accusative (invite someone to something)

options.note: Using быть откровенным с + instrumental (be frank with me)

Using один из + genitive (you're one of us), warmer

keyPoint: Начаться is perfective, denoting a single completed act of "starting" (pairs with начинаться).

grammarFocus.construction: nominative (урок) + adverb уже + perfective past (начался, reflexive masculine singular)
